## ===== devtools/seyoon/bootstrap-snapshot.sh =====

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bootstrap-snapshot.sh <worktree dir> <snapshot name> [--resume]
# Build a fresh olean snapshot of a worktree's Lean tree, for a session that has none (a new
# machine or cloud VM). It compiles every module the root TCSlib.lean imports (never the root
# itself) in dependency order (bootstrap_order.py), one at a time, through
# scripts/lean_check_tree.sh (no `lake build`), into $TCSLIB_SCRATCH/<snapshot name>. Modules that
# need a package with no compiled oleans (on the cloud machine, PFR) are left out with their
# importers, and listed in skipped-<name>.txt. Mathlib's oleans must already be in the worktree's
# .lake/packages (`lake exe cache get`, with Mathlib's cache hosts reachable). The log records
# the commit, each module's exit status, error and sorry counts, and the total; a failure stops
# the build. Record the snapshot with the commit it matches (the log's first line). The log's
# last line is exactly `# modules=N failed=0` when the build completes (what replay prechecks
# test).
#
# --resume continues a bootstrap that was killed (a cloud worker restart ends every process), or
# one that stopped on a module the order list now leaves out: the worktree's Lean tree
# (`TCSlib/`, `TCSlib.lean`) must be clean and equal to the log's commit's, the modules logged
# `exit=0` must be exactly a prefix of the (recomputed) order list with non-empty oleans, and a
# stopped run's failed module must be one the list now leaves out. It continues from the first
# module not logged (a killed module leaves no line), appending to the same log.
set -u
S="${TCSLIB_SCRATCH:-$HOME/.tcslib-scratch}"; WT=$S/$1; NAME=$2; O=$S/$NAME; MODE=${3:-}
T="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
[ -d "$WT/.lake/packages/mathlib/.lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib" ] || { echo "no Mathlib build in $WT/.lake/packages" >&2; exit 2; }
mkdir -p "$S/fills/replay"; LIST=$S/fills/replay/order-$NAME.txt; LOG=$S/fills/replay/bootstrap-$NAME.log
SKIP=$S/fills/replay/skipped-$NAME.txt
NOTE=""
case "$MODE" in
  "") [ -e "$O" ] && { echo "$O exists; choose a new name, or --resume" >&2; exit 2; }
      python3 -I "$T/bootstrap_order.py" "$WT" "$SKIP" > "$LIST" || exit 2
      : > "$LOG"; DONE=0 ;;
  --resume)
      [ -d "$O" ] && [ -f "$LOG" ] && [ -f "$LIST" ] || { echo "nothing to resume for $NAME" >&2; exit 2; }
      grep -q '^# modules=' "$LOG" && { echo "$NAME is complete"; tail -1 "$LOG"; exit 0; }
      C0=$(head -1 "$LOG" | sed -n 's/^# bootstrap [^ ]* at \([0-9a-f]\{40\}\) .*/\1/p')
      [ -n "$C0" ] || { echo "no commit on the log's first line" >&2; exit 2; }
      for p in TCSlib TCSlib.lean; do
        [ "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse "$C0:$p")" = "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse "HEAD:$p")" ] \
          || { echo "$p at HEAD differs from $C0" >&2; exit 2; }
      done
      [ -z "$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain -- TCSlib TCSlib.lean)" ] || { echo "uncommitted Lean changes in $WT" >&2; exit 2; }
      NEWLIST=$(mktemp); NEWSKIP=$(mktemp)
      python3 -I "$T/bootstrap_order.py" "$WT" "$NEWSKIP" > "$NEWLIST" || exit 2
      if grep -q '^# stopped' "$LOG"; then
        FAILED=$(grep -E ' exit=[1-9][0-9]* errors=' "$LOG" | tail -1 | cut -d' ' -f1)
        cut -f1 "$NEWSKIP" | grep -qx "$FAILED" \
          || { echo "$NAME stopped at $FAILED, which the order list still contains; start a new snapshot" >&2; exit 2; }
        NOTE="; the run had stopped at $FAILED, which the order list now leaves out"
      fi
      DONE=$(grep -c ' exit=0 errors=' "$LOG")
      [ "$(grep ' exit=0 errors=' "$LOG" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$(head -n "$DONE" "$NEWLIST")" ] \
        || { echo "the logged modules are not a prefix of the order list" >&2; exit 2; }
      while read -r m; do [ -s "$O/$m.olean" ] || { echo "missing olean for logged $m" >&2; exit 2; }; done < <(head -n "$DONE" "$NEWLIST")
      if ! cmp -s "$NEWLIST" "$LIST"; then
        cp "$LIST" "$LIST.prev"
        NOTE="$NOTE; the order list is recomputed ($(wc -l < "$LIST" | tr -d ' ') -> $(wc -l < "$NEWLIST" | tr -d ' ') modules; the previous one is $(basename "$LIST").prev)"
      fi
      mv "$NEWLIST" "$LIST"; mv "$NEWSKIP" "$SKIP"
      ;;
  *) echo "unknown option $MODE" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
cd "$WT" || exit 1
{ if [ "$DONE" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "# bootstrap $NAME at $(git rev-parse HEAD) ($(wc -l < "$LIST" | tr -d ' ') modules); $(date)"
  else
    echo "# resumed after $DONE modules, at $(git rev-parse HEAD) (same Lean tree)$NOTE; $(date)"
  fi
  [ -s "$SKIP" ] && echo "# left out: $(wc -l < "$SKIP" | tr -d ' ') modules that need a package without oleans ($(basename "$SKIP"))"
  n=$DONE
  while read -r m; do
    n=$((n+1))
    out=$(TCSLIB_OLEANS=$O nice -n 10 bash scripts/lean_check_tree.sh "$m" 2>&1); st=$?
    echo "$m exit=$st errors=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c "error") sorry=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c "declaration uses 'sorry'")"
    [ $st -ne 0 ] && { printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep error | head -5; echo "# stopped at $n"; exit 1; }
  done < <(tail -n +"$((DONE+1))" "$LIST")
  echo "# finished $(date)"
  echo "# modules=$n failed=0"; } >> "$LOG" 2>&1
tail -1 "$LOG"

## ===== devtools/seyoon/scratch-api/slotrun.sh =====

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# slotrun.sh <command…>: run a command that starts one Lean process at a time (a replay script,
# which calls scripts/lean_check_tree.sh and takes no slot itself) while holding a Lean slot.
# The machine-wide cap is five (user, 2026-11-06); TCSLIB_LEAN_SLOTS may set a smaller local
# budget for another campaign's separate locks. Waits silently; releases the slot on exit.
. "${TCSLIB_SCRATCH:?set TCSLIB_SCRATCH}/env.sh"
LOCKS=$TCSLIB_SCRATCH/locks; mkdir -p "$LOCKS"; SLOT=""
SLOT_LIMIT="${TCSLIB_LEAN_SLOTS:-5}"
case "$SLOT_LIMIT" in 1|2|3|4|5) ;; *) echo 'TCSLIB_LEAN_SLOTS must be 1..5' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
release() { if [ -n "$SLOT" ]; then rm -f "$SLOT/pid"; rmdir "$SLOT" 2>/dev/null; SLOT=""; fi; }
trap release EXIT
trap 'release; exit 130' INT TERM
while [ -z "$SLOT" ]; do
  for ((i=1; i<=SLOT_LIMIT; i++)); do
    s="$LOCKS/lean-slot-$i"
    if mkdir "$s" 2>/dev/null; then echo $$ > "$s/pid"; SLOT="$s"; break; fi
    p=$(cat "$s/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$p" ] && ! kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null; } || { [ -z "$p" ] && [ -n "$(find "$s" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +1 2>/dev/null)" ]; }; then
      rm -f "$s/pid"; rmdir "$s" 2>/dev/null
    fi
  done
  [ -z "$SLOT" ] && sleep 5
done
"$@"

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/PolyTimePairing.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTime
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Polynomial-time pairing, projections and branching

Closure facts for the function class FP (`Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`, implicit
throughout [AB09, ch. 2]) needed when a reduction must keep its input while computing
from it: constant functions, the threaded payload map, pairing of two polynomial-time
functions through `Turing.pairEncode`, the total pair projections, concatenation,
Boolean branching and length tests, and the unary length maps `x ↦ 1^|x|` and
`x ↦ 1^{C(|x|+1)^d}` (the input of a uniformity machine, [AB09, Def 6.12]). All are
assembled from the proved machine catalog of
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives`. The closure facts for the class `P`
built on them are in `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PClosure`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.pairMapSnd` — on `pairEncode a b`, output `pairEncode a (g b)`; malformed
  words go to `[]`.
* `Complexity.pairFstD`, `Complexity.pairSndD` — total pair projections (`[]` on
  malformed words).

## Main results

* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_of_linear` — a linear-time machine contract gives a
  polynomial-time computable function.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const` — constant functions are polynomial-time.
* `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairMapSnd` — the threaded payload map preserves
  polynomial time.
* `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode` — `x ↦ pairEncode (f x) (g x)` is
  polynomial-time when `f` and `g` are.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unary` — `x ↦ 1^|x|` is polynomial-time;
  `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary` — so is `x ↦ 1^{C(|x|+1)^d}`.
* `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append` — FP is closed under concatenation.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD`, `polyTimeComputable_pairSndD`,
  `polyTimeComputable_pairSwap`, `polyTimeComputable_pairConcat`,
  `polyTimeComputable_prepend` — projections and rearrangements of pairs.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite`, `polyTimeComputable_and` — Boolean branching.
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenLe`, `polyTimeComputable_lenEq` — length tests on
  pairs.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Ch. 2; §6.2, Definition 6.12.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- A function computed by a finite binary machine within a linear bound `a · (n + 1)`
is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_of_linear {f : List Bool → List Bool}
    (h : ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (a : ℕ), M.ComputesFunInTime f (fun n => a * (n + 1))) :
    PolyTimeComputable f := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, hM⟩ := h
  exact ⟨M, a, 1, by simpa only [Nat.pow_one] using hM⟩

/-- Every constant function `fun _ => w` is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_const (w : List Bool) : PolyTimeComputable (fun _ => w) :=
  polyTimeComputable_of_linear (FinTM.computesFunInTime_const w)

/-- The threaded payload map of `g`: on a pair `pairEncode a b` it outputs
`pairEncode a (g b)` (the first component is carried unchanged), and on a word that is
not a pair it outputs `[]`. -/
def pairMapSnd (g : List Bool → List Bool) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  match pairDecode z with
  | some (a, b) => pairEncode a (g b)
  | none => []

/-- On a pair, the threaded payload map transforms the second component. -/
@[simp]
theorem pairMapSnd_pairEncode (g : List Bool → List Bool) (a b : List Bool) :
    pairMapSnd g (pairEncode a b) = pairEncode a (g b) := by
  simp [pairMapSnd, pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- If `g` is polynomial-time computable, so is its threaded payload map
`Complexity.pairMapSnd g`.

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd` with the monotone
majorant `C (n+1)^c` of `g`'s bound gives a budget `K (n + 1 + C (n+1)^c)`, which is at
most `K (C + 1) (n+1)^(c+1)`. -/
theorem PolyTimeComputable.pairMapSnd {g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) : PolyTimeComputable (Complexity.pairMapSnd g) := by
  obtain ⟨G, C, c, hG⟩ := hg
  obtain ⟨M, K, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairMapSnd hG
    (by
      intro m n h
      exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left C (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (Nat.add_le_add_right h 1) c))
  refine ⟨M, K * (C + 1), c + 1, fun x => (hM x).mono ?_⟩
  have hn : x.length + 1 ≤ (x.length + 1) ^ (c + 1) := by
    simpa only [Nat.pow_one] using
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos x.length) (show 1 ≤ c + 1 by omega)
  have hc := Nat.mul_le_mul_left C
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos x.length) (Nat.le_succ c))
  calc
    _ ≤ K * ((x.length + 1) ^ (c + 1) + C * (x.length + 1) ^ (c + 1)) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left K (Nat.add_le_add hn hc)
    _ = _ := by ring

/-- Appending to a pair appends to its second component. -/
private lemma pairEncode_append (a b c : List Bool) :
    pairEncode a b ++ c = pairEncode a (b ++ c) := by
  simp [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]

/-- **Pairing two polynomial-time functions is polynomial-time**: if `f` and `g` are
polynomial-time computable, so is `x ↦ pairEncode (f x) (g x)`.

**Proof sketch.** Only the second component of a pair can be transformed in place
(`Complexity.pairMapSnd`), so the first component is built with an empty payload and
then retained. Duplicating `x` (`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairDup`) and mapping
the payload gives `H x = pairEncode (f x) []`; duplicating `x` and mapping `H` gives
`s x = pairEncode x (H x)`; duplicating `s x` and mapping `g ∘ fst` gives
`t x = pairEncode (s x) (g x)`. Concatenating the components of `t x`
(`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairConcat`) yields
`pairEncode x (pairEncode (f x) (g x))`, whose second component is the result. -/
theorem PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => Turing.pairEncode (f x) (g x)) := by
  have hd := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairDup
  have hp := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst
  have hs := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd
  have hc := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairConcat
  -- `H x = pairEncode (f x) []`, `s x = pairEncode x (H x)`, `t x = pairEncode (s x) (g x)`
  have hH := (((polyTimeComputable_const []).pairMapSnd).comp hd).comp hf
  have hS := hH.pairMapSnd.comp hd
  have hT := ((hg.comp hp).pairMapSnd.comp hd).comp hS
  -- concatenate, then project the second component
  have h := hs.comp (hc.comp hT)
  convert h using 1
  funext x
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, pairMapSnd_pairEncode, pairDecode_pairEncode,
    Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]
  rw [pairEncode_append, pairEncode_append]
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- The last `true` of `1^(n+1)` is its last letter: stripping it leaves `1ⁿ`. -/
private lemma splitAtLastTrue_replicate_succ (n : ℕ) :
    splitAtLastTrue (List.replicate (n + 1) true) = some (List.replicate n true) := by
  rw [splitAtLastTrue, List.reverse_replicate, List.replicate_succ]
  simp [List.reverse_replicate]

/-- **The unary length map is polynomial-time**: `x ↦ 1^|x|` is polynomial-time
computable. (This is how the input `1ⁿ` of a uniformity machine [AB09, Def 6.12] is
produced from an input of length `n`.)

**Proof sketch.** Pair `x` with `1^(|x|+1)` (the unary polynomial generator at
`1 · (n + 1)¹`, `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary`), strip the last `true` of the
second component (`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_stripLast`), and project the second
component (`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_unary :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => List.replicate x.length true) := by
  have hu : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => List.replicate (1 * (x.length + 1) ^ 1) true) := by
    obtain ⟨M, c, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary 1 1
    exact ⟨M, c, 2, hM⟩
  have hpair := polyTimeComputable_id.pairEncode hu
  have hstrip : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => match pairDecode x with
      | some (a, v) =>
        match splitAtLastTrue v with
        | some u => Turing.pairEncode a u
        | none => []
      | none => []) := by
    obtain ⟨M, c, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_stripLast
    exact ⟨M, c, 2, hM⟩
  have hs := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd
  convert hs.comp (hstrip.comp hpair) using 1
  funext x
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, id, pairDecode_pairEncode, Nat.pow_one, Nat.one_mul,
    splitAtLastTrue_replicate_succ, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]

/-- **FP is closed under concatenation**: if `f` and `g` are polynomial-time computable,
so is `x ↦ f x ++ g x`. (Pair the two results, `PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode`, then
concatenate the components, `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairConcat`.) -/
theorem PolyTimeComputable.append {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => f x ++ g x) := by
  have hc := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairConcat
  convert hc.comp (hf.pairEncode hg) using 1
  funext x
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- `x ↦ 1^{C (|x| + 1)^d}` is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_polyUnary (C d : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (C * (x.length + 1) ^ d) true := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary C d
  exact ⟨M, a, d + 1, hM⟩

/-- Prepending a fixed word is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_prepend (w : List Bool) : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => w ++ x) :=
  polyTimeComputable_of_linear (FinTM.computesFunInTime_prepend w)

/-! ### Total pair projections -/

/-- The total first projection of a `Turing.pairEncode` pair (`[]` on malformed words). -/
def pairFstD (z : List Bool) : List Bool := ((pairDecode z).map Prod.fst).getD []

/-- The total second projection of a `Turing.pairEncode` pair (`[]` on malformed words). -/
def pairSndD (z : List Bool) : List Bool := ((pairDecode z).map Prod.snd).getD []

/-- The first projection of a pair is its first component. -/
@[simp] theorem pairFstD_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) : pairFstD (pairEncode a b) = a := by
  simp [pairFstD, pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- The second projection of a pair is its second component. -/
@[simp] theorem pairSndD_pairEncode (a b : List Bool) : pairSndD (pairEncode a b) = b := by
  simp [pairSndD, pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- The first projection of a word is no longer than the word. -/
theorem length_pairFstD_le (z : List Bool) : (pairFstD z).length ≤ z.length := by
  cases h : pairDecode z with
  | none => simp [pairFstD, h]
  | some ab =>
    obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := ab
    have hz := Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z a b h
    subst hz
    simp [length_pairEncode]
    omega

/-- The first projection is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairFstD : PolyTimeComputable pairFstD :=
  polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst

/-- The second projection is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairSndD : PolyTimeComputable pairSndD :=
  polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd

/-- Iterated first projections (the root of a nested tuple) are polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_iterate_pairFstD (n : ℕ) : PolyTimeComputable (pairFstD^[n]) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp only [Function.iterate_zero]; exact polyTimeComputable_id
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ']
    exact polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp ih

/-- Concatenating the two components of a pair is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairConcat :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => pairFstD z ++ pairSndD z) := by
  have h := polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairConcat
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  cases hz : pairDecode z with
  | none => simp [pairFstD, pairSndD, hz]
  | some p => cases p; simp [pairFstD, pairSndD, hz]

/-- Swapping the components of a pair is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairSwap :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => pairEncode (pairSndD z) (pairFstD z)) :=
  polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD

/-! ### Branching and length tests -/

/-- **Polynomial-time branching**: if the test `p` (as a one-bit output) and both branches
are polynomial-time computable, so is `x ↦ if p x then f x else g x`.

**Proof sketch.** The timed branch contract `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond` runs
the test, then the selected branch; enlarge the three degrees to their maximum and
absorb the constants. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_ite {p : List Bool → Bool} {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hp : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x]))
    (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => if p x then f x else g x) := by
  obtain ⟨D, A, a, hD⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨F, B, b, hF⟩ := hf
  obtain ⟨G, C, c, hG⟩ := hg
  obtain ⟨M, K, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond hD hF hG
  let e := max a (max b c)
  refine ⟨M, K * (A + B + C + 1), e, fun x => (hM x).mono ?_⟩
  have hpow (d : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ e) : (x.length + 1) ^ d ≤ (x.length + 1) ^ e :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos _) hd
  have ha := Nat.mul_le_mul_left A (hpow a (Nat.le_max_left _ _))
  have hb := Nat.mul_le_mul_left B (hpow b
    ((Nat.le_max_left b c).trans (Nat.le_max_right a (max b c))))
  have hc := Nat.mul_le_mul_left C (hpow c
    ((Nat.le_max_right b c).trans (Nat.le_max_right a (max b c))))
  have hbc : max (B * (x.length + 1) ^ b) (C * (x.length + 1) ^ c) ≤
      B * (x.length + 1) ^ e + C * (x.length + 1) ^ e :=
    max_le (by omega) (by omega)
  have hone := Nat.one_le_pow e (x.length + 1) (Nat.succ_pos _)
  calc
    _ ≤ K * (A * (x.length + 1) ^ e +
        (B * (x.length + 1) ^ e + C * (x.length + 1) ^ e) +
        (x.length + 1) ^ e) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left K (Nat.add_le_add (Nat.add_le_add ha hbc) hone)
    _ = _ := by ring

/-- Polynomial-time Boolean conjunction of two one-bit tests. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_and {p q : List Bool → Bool}
    (hp : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x])) (hq : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [q x])) :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [p x && q x]) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_ite hp hq (polyTimeComputable_const [false]) using 1
  funext x
  cases p x <;> rfl

/-- The length test `|snd z| ≤ |fst z|` on pairs is polynomial-time.

**Proof sketch.** The catalog's threaded length check at `(C, e) = (1, 1)` decides
`|b| ≤ |a| + 1` on `⟨a, b⟩`; apply it to `⟨fst z, 1 :: snd z⟩`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_lenLe :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [decide ((pairSndD z).length ≤ (pairFstD z).length)]) := by
  have hchk : PolyTimeComputable (fun x => [match pairDecode x with
      | some (a, b) => decide (b.length ≤ 1 * (a.length + 1) ^ 1)
      | none => false]) := by
    obtain ⟨M, a, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairLenCheck 1 1
    exact ⟨M, a, 2, hM⟩
  have hpair : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => pairEncode (pairFstD z) (true :: pairSndD z)) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
      ((polyTimeComputable_prepend [true]).comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  convert hchk.comp hpair using 1
  funext z
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- The length-equality test `|fst z| = |snd z|` on pairs is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_lenEq :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [decide ((pairFstD z).length = (pairSndD z).length)]) := by
  have h := polyTimeComputable_and polyTimeComputable_lenLe
    (polyTimeComputable_lenLe.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSwap)
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
  congr 1
  by_cases h1 : (pairFstD z).length = (pairSndD z).length
  · simp [h1]
  · rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne h1 with h2 | h2
    · simp [h1, Nat.not_le_of_lt h2]
    · simp [h1, Nat.not_le_of_lt h2]

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Basic.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.DTIME
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Space-bounded computation, `SPACE`, `L`, and implicitly logspace computable functions

[AB09, Def 4.1]: a language is in `SPACE(s(n))` when some machine decides it while
visiting at most `c · s(n)` work-tape cells on every input of length `n`; `L = SPACE(log n)`
[AB09, Def 4.5]. [AB09, Def 4.16]: a function `f` is *implicitly logspace computable* when it
is polynomially bounded and the two languages "the `i`-th bit of `f(x)` is `1`" and
"`i` is a position of `f(x)`" are in `L`.

## The machine model

We reuse the campaign's machines (`Turing.FinTM Bool`) unchanged. They already have the
shape of [AB09, Fig. 4.1]:

* **the input tape is read-only**: a transition (`Turing.Action`) has no write component
  for the input tape, only a head move, clamped to the input and its two boundary blanks;
* **the output tape is write-once, append-only**: a step appends at most one symbol;
* **space is the number of work-tape cells visited** (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed`, the
  sum over the work tapes of the visited cells), exactly the measure of [AB09, Def 4.1]
  ("at most `c · s(n)` locations on M's work tapes (excluding the input tape) are ever
  visited by M's head").

## Main definitions

* `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace` — `M` computes `f`, halting on every input, visiting at most
  `s(|x|)` work cells.
* `Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace` — `M` decides `L` within space `s`. [AB09, Def 4.1]
* `Complexity.SPACE` — the class of languages decidable in space `c · s(n)`. [AB09, Def 4.1]
* `Complexity.logSpace` — the logarithmic space bound `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`.
* `Complexity.LOGSPACE` — the class `L = SPACE(log n)`. [AB09, Def 4.5]
* `Complexity.indexLang` — the language `{⟨x, i⟩ | p x i}` with `i` in binary.
* `Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable` — [AB09, Def 4.16].

## Main results

* `Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_iff`, `Complexity.logSpace_eq` — the definitions of
  `ComputesInSpace` and `logSpace` as an equivalence and an equation.
* `Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff`, `Complexity.mem_SPACE_iff`, `Complexity.LOGSPACE_eq` —
  the definitions of `DecidesInSpace`, `SPACE` and `LOGSPACE`, unfolded.
* `Complexity.SPACE.mono` — `SPACE` is monotone in the space bound.
* `Complexity.logSpace_le_succ`, `Complexity.logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow` — the logarithmic
  bound is at most linear, and at most `(A + 1) s` below `A · 2^s`.
* `Complexity.logSpace_le_size_succ` — the logarithmic bound is at most one more than the
  binary length.
* `Complexity.SPACE.mono_const` — `SPACE` absorbs constant factors (added 2026-10-10).
* `Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero` — no work tapes, zero space (added
  2026-10-10).

## Divergences from [AB09]

* **The logarithm.** [AB09] writes `SPACE(log n)` and requires `s(n) ≥ log n` (p. 79). We use
  `logSpace n = ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`, which is at least `1` (so short inputs get constant space, the
  standard reading of the convention) and is `Θ(log n)` for `n ≥ 2`.
* **Pairs and indices** (Def 4.16). The pair `⟨x, i⟩` is `Turing.pairEncode x (Nat.bits i)`:
  the campaign's self-delimiting pairing with the index in little-endian binary without
  redundant zeros (`Nat.bits 0 = []`). Indices are **`0`-based**: the bit language is
  `{⟨x, i⟩ | f(x)ᵢ = 1}` with `f(x)ᵢ` the `i`-th bit from `0`, and the length language is
  `{⟨x, i⟩ | i < |f(x)|}` where [AB09] writes `i ≤ |f(x)|` for `1`-based `i`.
* **Polynomial bound** (Def 4.16). [AB09] asks `|f(x)| ≤ |x|^c`; at `x = ε` that forces
  `f(ε) = ε` for `c ≥ 1`. We use the campaign normal form `|f(x)| ≤ C · (|x| + 1)^c`
  (`Complexity.PolyBound` shape).
* **Halting.** Deciding (resp. computing) includes halting on every input, as in [AB09]
  ("a TM M deciding L"); the space bound is checked at the halting time, and since space is
  monotone in time and frozen after halting this is the space of the whole computation.
* **One measure for both classes.** [AB09, Def 4.1]'s own wording splits: *visited*
  work-tape locations for `SPACE` (the clause quoted above) but *nonblank* locations for
  `NSPACE`. The campaign convention is the visited-cells measure for both; the planned
  `NSPACE` (`AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`, phase P4.1) counts visited cells along every
  choice word, with all branches halting.
* **Zero bounds collapse the class** (P0 reception audit, round 1, finding 1): every
  work tape's visited set contains its origin, so every machine satisfies
  `M.k ≤ spaceUsed` on every input at every time. A single length with `s n = 0`
  therefore forces a deciding machine to have **no work tapes at all** — and then it
  has zero space on *every* input — so `SPACE s = SPACE (fun _ => 0)` (semantically
  the two-way-finite-automaton class) whenever `s` has a zero; multiplicative
  absorption cannot repair this, since `c * 0 = 0`. In particular the literal
  `SPACE (fun n => n)` is **not** linear space: `n = 0` collapses it. **Campaign
  convention:** every asymptotic chapter statement uses an everywhere-positive bound —
  `fun n => n + 1`, `fun n => n ^ c + 1`, `Complexity.logSpace` — never a bound with a
  zero. The characterization and the harmless-normalization identities are the sanity
  layer `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ZeroSpace`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1, Definitions 4.1 and 4.5; §4.3, Definition 4.16.)
-/

namespace Turing.FinTM

/-- The machine `M` computes `f` in space `s`: on every input `x` it halts with output `f x`,
and up to that time it has visited at most `s |x|` work-tape cells (summed over its work
tapes). The input tape (read-only) and the output tape (append-only) do not count.
[AB09, Def 4.1, for functions] -/
def ComputesInSpace (M : FinTM Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t, M.ComputesInTime x (f x) t ∧
    M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ s x.length

/-- **Computing in space, unfolded**: `M` computes `f` in space `s` exactly when on every input
`x` there is a time `t` at which `M` has halted with output `f x`
(`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime`), having visited at most `s |x|` work-tape cells by then. -/
theorem computesInSpace_iff (M : FinTM Bool) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (s : ℕ → ℕ) :
    M.ComputesInSpace f s ↔
      ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t, M.ComputesInTime x (f x) t ∧
        M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ s x.length :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The machine `M` decides `L` in space `s`: it computes the indicator `[x ∈ L]` (a
one-bit output) in space `s`. [AB09, Def 4.1] -/
def DecidesInSpace (M : FinTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  M.ComputesInSpace (fun x => [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x]) s

/-- **Deciding in space, unfolded**: `M` decides `L` in space `s` exactly when it computes the
one-bit indicator `x ↦ [x ∈ L]` in space `s`. -/
theorem decidesInSpace_iff (M : FinTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (s : ℕ → ℕ) :
    M.DecidesInSpace L s ↔
      M.ComputesInSpace (fun x => [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x]) s :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- A space bound can be weakened. -/
theorem ComputesInSpace.mono {M : FinTM Bool} {f : List Bool → List Bool} {s s' : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : M.ComputesInSpace f s) (hs : ∀ n, s n ≤ s' n) : M.ComputesInSpace f s' := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hsp⟩ := h x
  exact ⟨t, ht, hsp.trans (hs _)⟩

/-- A machine with no work tapes computes in zero space whatever it computes at all: the
space measure counts only work-tape cells. (Shared by the zero-space layer; added
2026-10-10.)

**Proof sketch.** With `M.k = 0` the space measure is an empty sum
(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_zero_tapes_eq_zero`), at every halting time. -/
theorem computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero {M : FinTM Bool} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hk : M.k = 0) (h : ∀ x, ∃ t, M.ComputesInTime x (f x) t) :
    M.ComputesInSpace f fun _ => 0 := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h x
  exact ⟨t, ht, (MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_zero_tapes_eq_zero (tm := M.tm) _ t hk).le⟩

end Turing.FinTM

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- **`SPACE(s)`** [AB09, Def 4.1]: the languages decided by some finite binary-alphabet
machine visiting at most `c · s(n)` work-tape cells on inputs of length `n`, for some
constant `c`. -/
def SPACE (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (Language Bool) :=
  {L | ∃ (c : ℕ) (M : FinTM Bool), M.DecidesInSpace L fun n => c * s n}

/-- **Membership in `SPACE`, unfolded**: `L ∈ SPACE s` exactly when some machine decides `L` in
space `c · s` for some constant `c`. -/
theorem mem_SPACE_iff {s : ℕ → ℕ} {L : Language Bool} :
    L ∈ SPACE s ↔ ∃ (c : ℕ) (M : FinTM Bool), M.DecidesInSpace L fun n => c * s n :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- `SPACE` is monotone in the space bound. -/
theorem SPACE.mono {s₁ s₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ n, s₁ n ≤ s₂ n) : SPACE s₁ ⊆ SPACE s₂ := by
  rintro L ⟨c, M, hM⟩
  exact ⟨c, M, hM.mono fun n => Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h n)⟩

/-- `SPACE` absorbs constant factors: if `s₁ ≤ a · s₂` pointwise, then
`SPACE s₁ ⊆ SPACE s₂`. [AB09, Def 4.1: the constant `c` absorbs `a`] (Shared by the
zero-space layer and the hierarchy arguments; added 2026-10-10.)

**Proof sketch.** A witness at constant `c` for `s₁` is a witness at constant `c · a`
for `s₂`, since `c · s₁ n ≤ c · (a · s₂ n) = (c · a) · s₂ n`
(`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono`). -/
theorem SPACE.mono_const {s₁ s₂ : ℕ → ℕ} {a : ℕ} (h : ∀ n, s₁ n ≤ a * s₂ n) :
    SPACE s₁ ⊆ SPACE s₂ := by
  rintro L ⟨c, M, hM⟩
  refine ⟨c * a, M, hM.mono fun n => ?_⟩
  calc c * s₁ n ≤ c * (a * s₂ n) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h n)
    _ = c * a * s₂ n := (Nat.mul_assoc c a (s₂ n)).symm

/-- The logarithmic space bound `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`: `Θ(log n)`, and at least `1`, following the
convention `s(n) ≥ log n` of [AB09, p. 79]. -/
def logSpace (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log 2 n + 1

/-- The logarithmic bound's formula: `logSpace n = Nat.log 2 n + 1`. -/
theorem logSpace_eq (n : ℕ) : logSpace n = Nat.log 2 n + 1 := rfl

/-- The logarithmic bound is at most linear: `logSpace n ≤ n + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** `Nat.log 2 n ≤ n` (`Nat.log_le_self`), then `Complexity.logSpace_eq`. -/
theorem logSpace_le_succ (n : ℕ) : logSpace n ≤ n + 1 := by
  have := Nat.log_le_self 2 n
  rw [logSpace_eq]
  omega

/-- The logarithmic width is at most one more than the binary length:
`logSpace n ≤ Nat.size n + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** At `n = 0` both sides are `1`. Otherwise `2 ^ Nat.log 2 n ≤ n < 2 ^ Nat.size n`
(`Nat.pow_log_le_self`, `Nat.lt_size_self`), so `Nat.log 2 n < Nat.size n`. -/
lemma logSpace_le_size_succ (n : ℕ) : logSpace n ≤ Nat.size n + 1 := by
  unfold logSpace
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with h | h
  · subst h; simp
  · have h1 : 2 ^ Nat.log 2 n ≤ n := Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 (by omega)
    have h2 : n < 2 ^ Nat.size n := Nat.lt_size_self n
    have : Nat.log 2 n < Nat.size n :=
      (Nat.pow_lt_pow_iff_right (show 1 < 2 by norm_num)).mp (lt_of_le_of_lt h1 h2)
    omega

/-- A number at most `A · 2^s` (with `s ≥ 1`) has `logSpace` at most `(A + 1) s`. -/
theorem logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow {v A s : ℕ} (h : v ≤ A * 2 ^ s) (hs : 1 ≤ s) :
    logSpace v ≤ (A + 1) * s := by
  have hA : A < 2 ^ A := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have hlt : v < 2 ^ (A + s) := by
    rw [pow_add]
    exact lt_of_le_of_lt h (Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hA (Nat.two_pow_pos s))
  have hle : A + s ≤ (A + 1) * s := by
    have := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right A (show 0 < s by omega)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]; omega
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos v with rfl | hv
  · simp only [logSpace, Nat.log_zero_right]; omega
  · have := Nat.log_lt_of_lt_pow (by omega) hlt
    simp only [logSpace]; omega

/-- **The class `L`** [AB09, Def 4.5]: `L = SPACE(log n)`, the languages decidable by a
machine visiting `O(log n)` work-tape cells. (Named `LOGSPACE` to keep the letter `L` free
for language variables.) -/
def LOGSPACE : Set (Language Bool) := SPACE logSpace

/-- `LOGSPACE` is `SPACE logSpace`. -/
theorem LOGSPACE_eq : LOGSPACE = SPACE logSpace := rfl

/-- The language `{⟨x, i⟩ | p x i}`, the pair encoded as `Turing.pairEncode x (Nat.bits i)`
(index in little-endian binary). The shape of the two languages of [AB09, Def 4.16]. -/
def indexLang (p : List Bool → ℕ → Prop) : Language Bool :=
  {w | ∃ x i, w = pairEncode x (Nat.bits i) ∧ p x i}

/-- **Implicitly logspace computable functions** [AB09, Def 4.16]: `f` is polynomially
bounded, `|f(x)| ≤ C · (|x| + 1)^c`, and both the bit language
`{⟨x, i⟩ | f(x)ᵢ = 1}` and the length language `{⟨x, i⟩ | i < |f(x)|}` are in `L`.
Indices are `0`-based and written in binary (`Nat.bits`); see the module docstring for the
divergences (`0`-based `i < |f(x)|` for the book's `1`-based `i ≤ |f(x)|`, and the `+ 1`
in the polynomial bound). -/
def ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable (f : List Bool → List Bool) : Prop :=
  (∃ C c : ℕ, ∀ x : List Bool, (f x).length ≤ C * (x.length + 1) ^ c) ∧
  indexLang (fun x i => (f x).getD i false = true) ∈ LOGSPACE ∧
  indexLang (fun x i => i < (f x).length) ∈ LOGSPACE

/-- `logSpace` is monotone. -/
lemma logSpace_mono {a b : ℕ} (h : a ≤ b) : logSpace a ≤ logSpace b := by
  unfold logSpace
  have := Nat.log_mono_right (b := 2) h
  omega

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Codec/Engine.lean =====

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMLoops

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Abstract-register-machine fragments for the codec checkers

Bounded loops of abstract register machines (`Complexity.LogProg.ARM`) used by the logspace
checkers of the configuration codec, stated like the shared fragments of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess` (`registerCopy_loop`,
`registerScale_loop`, …): over any machine whose instructions at the given labels have the
given shape, as runs `Complexity.LogProg.AReach` through configurations meeting the syntactic
preconditions with all registers bounded by `B`.

* `Complexity.Codec.incChain`, `Complexity.Codec.decChain` — straight chains of increments
  and decrements of one register.
* `Complexity.Codec.scan_loop` — **the scan engine**: walk two pointers through the input in
  lockstep (any stride), read the input bit under each through a bit oracle, and feed the
  pair of bits to a finite-state step; the run ends in the label of the fold of the step
  over the zipped words read.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeStride_loop` — decode a binary field laid out at any stride
  (most significant letter last), `boundedDecodeStride_loop`.
* `Complexity.Codec.halvCount_loop` — count the binary digits of a register by halving.
* `Complexity.Codec.le_loop` — compare two registers by counting.

Logspace machine infrastructure ([AB09, §4.1: logspace algorithms keep a constant number of
`O(log n)`-bit counters]); not a result of [AB09].

The chains and the stride decoder are those of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess`: `incChain` and `decChain` are the two
directions of `Complexity.LogProg.arm_chain`, and `decodeStride_loop` is
`Complexity.LogProg.boundedDecodeStride_loop` (the codec's fields are doubled in the virtual
input, so it reads at stride two), all stated here through the guard `GuardLe`.

## Main definitions

* none (run theorems for bounded loops of `Complexity.LogProg.ARM`).

## Main results

* `Complexity.Codec.incChain`, `Complexity.Codec.decChain`.
* `Complexity.Codec.scan_loop`, `Complexity.Codec.decodeStride_loop`,
  `Complexity.Codec.halvCount_loop`, `Complexity.Codec.le_loop`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.)
-/

namespace Complexity.Codec

open Turing LogProg

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type}

/-- **A chain of increments** of register `r` along the labels `labels 0, …, labels k`.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.LogProg.arm_chain` with `up = true`. -/
theorem incChain (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (y : List Bool)
    (r : Fin m) (labels : ℕ → Λ) (k B : ℕ)
    (hcode : ∀ i < k, A (labels i) = .inc r (labels (i + 1)))
    (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hk : v r + k ≤ B) :
    AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some (labels 0), v, none)
      (some (labels k), Function.update v r (v r + k), none) :=
  arm_chain A oracle y r true labels k B hcode v hv hk

/-- **A chain of decrements** of register `r` along the labels `labels 0, …, labels k`
(with `k ≤ v r`, so no decrement truncates).

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.LogProg.arm_chain` with `up = false`. -/
theorem decChain (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (y : List Bool)
    (r : Fin m) (labels : ℕ → Λ) (k B : ℕ)
    (hcode : ∀ i < k, A (labels i) = .dec r (labels (i + 1)))
    (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hk : k ≤ v r) :
    AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some (labels 0), v, none)
      (some (labels k), Function.update v r (v r - k), none) :=
  arm_chain A oracle y r false labels k B hcode v hv hk

/-- **The scan engine.** Two pointer registers `p`, `q` walk in lockstep with stride
`stride` until `p` reaches `lim`; at each position the bits `u_i`, `u'_i` under the pointers
are read through the oracle `j` and the finite-state step `δ` consumes the pair. The run from
`test st₀` ends in `done` of the fold of `δ` over the zipped words, with both pointers
advanced by `stride · |u|`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `u` (with `u'` of the same length). If `p = lim` the run
exits; otherwise the two reads take the bits `u_0`, `u'_0`, the step applies `δ`, and two
increment chains (`incChain`) advance the pointers to the rest of the words. Pointer values
stay below `lim` (for `p`) and the supplied bound (for `q`). -/
theorem scan_loop {σ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (y : List Bool) (p q lim : Fin m) (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpl : p ≠ lim) (hql : q ≠ lim) (j : Fin d)
    (δ : σ → Bool × Bool → σ) (test rd1 : σ → Λ) (rd2 : σ → Bool → Λ) (adv1 adv2 : σ → ℕ → Λ)
    (done : σ → Λ) (stride : ℕ) (hs : 0 < stride)
    (htest : ∀ st, A (test st) = .jeq p lim (done st) (rd1 st))
    (hrd1 : ∀ st, A (rd1 st) = .call j .whole [p] (rd2 st true) (rd2 st false))
    (hrd2 : ∀ st b, A (rd2 st b) =
      .call j .whole [q] (adv1 (δ st (b, true)) 0) (adv1 (δ st (b, false)) 0))
    (hadv1 : ∀ st i, i < stride → A (adv1 st i) = .inc p (adv1 st (i + 1)))
    (hend1 : ∀ st, adv1 st stride = adv2 st 0)
    (hadv2 : ∀ st i, i < stride → A (adv2 st i) = .inc q (adv2 st (i + 1)))
    (hend2 : ∀ st, adv2 st stride = test st)
    (B : ℕ) (u u' : List Bool) (hlen : u'.length = u.length) (st₀ : σ) (v : Fin m → ℕ)
    (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B) (hlim : v lim = v p + stride * u.length)
    (hq : v q + stride * u.length ≤ B)
    (ho1 : ∀ i < u.length, oracle j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits (v p + stride * i))) = u.getD i false)
    (ho2 : ∀ i < u.length, oracle j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits (v q + stride * i))) =
      u'.getD i false) :
    AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some (test st₀), v, none)
      (some (done ((List.zip u u').foldl δ st₀)),
        Function.update (Function.update v p (v p + stride * u.length)) q
          (v q + stride * u.length), none) := by
  induction u generalizing u' st₀ v with
  | nil =>
    have e : v p = v lim := by simpa using hlim.symm
    have hu' : u' = [] := List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by simpa using hlen)
    subst hu'
    simp only [List.zip_nil_left, List.foldl_nil, List.length_nil, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero,
      Function.update_eq_self]
    simpa [astep_jeq (htest st₀), e] using
      (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := y) (G := GuardLe A y B)
        (a := (some (test st₀), v, none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, htest, hpl], hv⟩)
  | cons b u ih =>
    obtain ⟨b', u'', rfl⟩ : ∃ b' u'', u' = b' :: u'' := by
      cases u' with
      | nil => simp at hlen
      | cons b' u'' => exact ⟨b', u'', rfl⟩
    simp only [List.length_cons] at hlen hlim hq
    have hstep : stride ≤ stride * (u.length + 1) :=
      Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right stride (by omega)
    have hne : v p ≠ v lim := by omega
    have hb := ho1 0 (by simp)
    have hb' := ho2 0 (by simp)
    simp only [Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero, List.getD_cons_zero] at hb hb'
    set st₁ := δ st₀ (b, b') with hst₁
    -- the test and the two reads
    have reads : AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some (test st₀), v, none)
        (some (adv1 st₁ 0), v, none) := by
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, htest, hpl], hv⟩
      simp only [astep_jeq (htest st₀), if_neg hne]
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hrd1], hv⟩
      simp only [astep_call (hrd1 st₀), vword_whole₁, hb]
      have e1 : (if b = true then rd2 st₀ true else rd2 st₀ false) = rd2 st₀ b := by
        cases b <;> rfl
      rw [e1]
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hrd2], hv⟩
      simp only [astep_call (hrd2 st₀ b), vword_whole₁, hb']
      have e2 : (if b' = true then adv1 (δ st₀ (b, true)) 0 else adv1 (δ st₀ (b, false)) 0) =
          adv1 st₁ 0 := by cases b' <;> rfl
      rw [e2]
      exact AReach.refl _
    -- the two increment chains
    set v₁ := Function.update v p (v p + stride) with hv₁
    set v₂ := Function.update v₁ q (v q + stride) with hv₂
    have bd₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := register_update_le v p B _ hv (by have := hv lim; omega)
    have bd₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := register_update_le v₁ q B _ bd₁ (by omega)
    have c1 := incChain A oracle y p (adv1 st₁) stride B (hadv1 st₁) v hv
      (by have := hv lim; omega)
    rw [hend1] at c1
    have c2 := incChain A oracle y q (adv2 st₁) stride B (hadv2 st₁) v₁ bd₁
      (by rw [hv₁, Function.update_of_ne hpq.symm]; omega)
    rw [hend2, hv₁, Function.update_of_ne hpq.symm] at c2
    -- the rest of the words
    have v₂p : v₂ p = v p + stride := by
      rw [hv₂, Function.update_of_ne hpq, hv₁, Function.update_self]
    have v₂q : v₂ q = v q + stride := by rw [hv₂, Function.update_self]
    have v₂l : v₂ lim = v lim := by
      rw [hv₂, Function.update_of_ne hql.symm, hv₁, Function.update_of_ne hpl.symm]
    have rest := ih u'' (by simpa using hlen) st₁ v₂ bd₂
      (by rw [v₂l, v₂p, hlim]; ring)
      (by rw [v₂q]; rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at hq; omega)
      (fun i hi => by
        have := ho1 (i + 1) (by simp; omega)
        rw [v₂p, show v p + stride + stride * i = v p + stride * (i + 1) by ring, this]
        rfl)
      (fun i hi => by
        have := ho2 (i + 1) (by simp; omega)
        rw [v₂q, show v q + stride + stride * i = v q + stride * (i + 1) by ring, this]
        rfl)
    have fin : Function.update (Function.update v₂ p (v₂ p + stride * u.length)) q
        (v₂ q + stride * u.length) =
        Function.update (Function.update v p (v p + stride * (u.length + 1))) q
          (v q + stride * (u.length + 1)) := by
      rw [v₂p, v₂q]
      funext r
      by_cases hrq : r = q
      · subst hrq; simp only [Function.update_self]; ring
      · by_cases hrp : r = p
        · subst hrp
          simp only [Function.update_of_ne hrq, Function.update_self]; ring
        · simp [Function.update_of_ne hrq, Function.update_of_ne hrp, hv₂, hv₁]
    rw [fin] at rest
    simp only [List.zip_cons_cons, List.foldl_cons, List.length_cons]
    exact reads.trans (c1.trans (c2.trans rest))

/-- **A strided reverse scan decodes a bounded binary field** laid out at positions
`base + stride · i` (least significant letter first): from the pointer at
`base + stride · k`, with the suffix value from letter `k` in the accumulator, the run
reaches `done` with the value of the whole field.

**Proof sketch.** The stride decoder `Complexity.LogProg.boundedDecodeStride_loop` of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess`, whose guard is `GuardLe`. -/
theorem decodeStride_loop (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (y : List Bool) (ptr base acc tmp : Fin m)
    (hpb : ptr ≠ base) (hpa : ptr ≠ acc) (hpt : ptr ≠ tmp)
    (hba : base ≠ acc) (hbt : base ≠ tmp) (hat : acc ≠ tmp)
    (j : Fin d) (test read done : Λ) (downs : ℕ → Λ)
    (copy bump clear scale take add : Bool → Λ) (incs : Bool → ℕ → Λ) (stride : ℕ)
    (htest : A test = .jeq ptr base done (downs 0))
    (hdowns : ∀ i < stride, A (downs i) = .dec ptr (downs (i + 1)))
    (hdend : downs stride = read)
    (hread : A read = .call j .whole [ptr] (copy true) (copy false))
    (hcopy : ∀ b, A (copy b) = .jeq tmp acc (clear b) (bump b))
    (hbump : ∀ b, A (bump b) = .inc tmp (copy b))
    (hclear : ∀ b, A (clear b) = .clr acc (scale b))
    (hscale : ∀ b, A (scale b) = .jz tmp (add b) (take b))
    (htake : ∀ b, A (take b) = .dec tmp (incs b 0))
    (hincs : ∀ b i, i < 2 → A (incs b i) = .inc acc (incs b (i + 1)))
    (hend : ∀ b, incs b 2 = scale b)
    (hadd : ∀ b, A (add b) = if b then .inc acc test else .jz tmp test test)
    (w : List Bool) (B : ℕ) (values : ∀ i ≤ w.length, bitsVal (w.drop i) ≤ B)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ w.length) (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B) (hs : 0 < stride)
    (hp : v ptr = v base + stride * k) (ha : v acc = bitsVal (w.drop k)) (ht : v tmp = 0)
    (ho : ∀ i < w.length,
      oracle j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits (v base + stride * i))) = w.getD i false) :
    ∃ v', (∀ r, v' r ≤ B) ∧ v' ptr = v base ∧ v' acc = bitsVal w ∧ v' tmp = 0 ∧
      (∀ r, r ≠ ptr → r ≠ acc → r ≠ tmp → v' r = v r) ∧
      AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some test, v, none) (some done, v', none) :=
  boundedDecodeStride_loop A oracle y ptr base acc tmp hpb hpa hpt hba hbt hat j test read done
    downs copy bump clear scale take add incs stride htest hdowns hdend hread hcopy hbump hclear
    hscale htake hincs hend hadd w B values k hk v hv hs hp ha ht ho

/-- **Counting binary digits by halving**: halving `t` until it is zero while incrementing
`c` adds `|bits t|` to `c` and clears `t`.

**Proof sketch.** Strong induction on the value of `t`: a nonzero value loses exactly one
binary digit when halved (`Complexity.LogProg.access_width_half`). -/
theorem halvCount_loop (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (y : List Bool)
    (t c : Fin m) (htc : t ≠ c) (test halve bump done : Λ)
    (htest : A test = .jz t done halve) (hhalve : A halve = .half t bump)
    (hbump : A bump = .inc c test) (B : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B)
    (hc : v c + (Nat.bits (v t)).length ≤ B) :
    AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some test, v, none)
      (some done, Function.update (Function.update v t 0) c (v c + (Nat.bits (v t)).length),
        none) := by
  generalize hn : v t = n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing v with
  | _ n ih =>
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hpos
    · have e : Function.update (Function.update v t 0) c (v c + (Nat.bits 0).length) = v := by
        funext r
        by_cases hrc : r = c
        · subst hrc; simp
        · by_cases hrt : r = t
          · subst hrt; simp [hrc, hn]
          · simp [hrc, hrt]
      rw [e]
      simpa [astep_jz htest, hn] using
        (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := y) (G := GuardLe A y B)
          (a := (some test, v, none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, htest], hv⟩)
    · rw [hn] at hc
      have hlen : (Nat.bits (n / 2)).length + 1 = (Nat.bits n).length :=
        access_width_half n (Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hpos)
      set v₁ := Function.update v t (n / 2)
      set v₂ := Function.update v₁ c (v c + 1)
      have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := register_update_le v t B _ hv (by have := hv t; omega)
      have b₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := register_update_le v₁ c B _ b₁ (by omega)
      have v₂t : v₂ t = n / 2 := by simp [v₂, v₁, htc]
      have v₂c : v₂ c = v c + 1 := by simp [v₂]
      have rest := ih (n / 2) (by omega) v₂ b₂ (by rw [v₂c, v₂t]; omega) v₂t
      have e : Function.update (Function.update v₂ t 0) c (v₂ c + (Nat.bits (n / 2)).length) =
          Function.update (Function.update v t 0) c (v c + (Nat.bits n).length) := by
        rw [v₂c]
        funext r
        by_cases hrc : r = c
        · subst hrc; simp; omega
        · by_cases hrt : r = t
          · subst hrt; simp [hrc]
          · simp [hrc, hrt, v₂, v₁]
      rw [e] at rest
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, htest], hv⟩
      simp only [astep_jz htest, hn, show n ≠ 0 by omega, ↓reduceIte]
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hhalve], hv⟩
      simp only [astep_half hhalve, hn]
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hbump], b₁⟩
      simp only [astep_inc hbump]
      have : Function.update v₁ c (v₁ c + 1) = v₂ := by simp [v₂, v₁, htc.symm]
      rw [this]
      exact rest

/-- **Comparing two registers by counting**: stepping `t` up from below both `a` and `b`
reaches `a` first (or simultaneously) iff `a ≤ b`; the run ends in `yes` or `no`
accordingly, with `t = min a b`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `min a b - t`: at `t = a` answer yes, else at `t = b`
answer no, else increment `t`. -/
theorem le_loop (A : ARM m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (y : List Bool)
    (t a b : Fin m) (hta : t ≠ a) (htb : t ≠ b) (test₁ test₂ bump yes no : Λ)
    (htest₁ : A test₁ = .jeq t a yes test₂) (htest₂ : A test₂ = .jeq t b no bump)
    (hbump : A bump = .inc t test₁) (B : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B)
    (ha : v t ≤ v a) (hb : v t ≤ v b) :
    AReach A oracle y (GuardLe A y B) (some test₁, v, none)
      (some (if v a ≤ v b then yes else no), Function.update v t (min (v a) (v b)), none) := by
  generalize hn : min (v a) (v b) - v t = n
  induction n generalizing v with
  | zero =>
    have hm : v t = min (v a) (v b) := by omega
    by_cases hab : v a ≤ v b
    · have eq : v t = v a := by omega
      rw [if_pos hab, ← hm, Function.update_eq_self]
      simpa [astep_jeq htest₁, eq] using
        (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := y) (G := GuardLe A y B)
          (a := (some test₁, v, none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, htest₁, hta], hv⟩)
    · have ne : v t ≠ v a := by omega
      have eq : v t = v b := by omega
      rw [if_neg hab, ← hm, Function.update_eq_self]
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, htest₁, hta], hv⟩
      simp only [astep_jeq htest₁, if_neg ne]
      simpa [astep_jeq htest₂, eq] using
        (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := y) (G := GuardLe A y B)
          (a := (some test₂, v, none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, htest₂, htb], hv⟩)
  | succ n ih =>
    have ne₁ : v t ≠ v a := by omega
    have ne₂ : v t ≠ v b := by omega
    set v₁ := Function.update v t (v t + 1)
    have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := register_update_le v t B _ hv (by have := hv a; omega)
    have va : v₁ a = v a := by simp [v₁, hta.symm]
    have vb : v₁ b = v b := by simp [v₁, htb.symm]
    have vt : v₁ t = v t + 1 := by simp [v₁]
    have rest := ih v₁ b₁ (by omega) (by omega) (by rw [va, vb, vt]; omega)
    rw [va, vb, show Function.update v₁ t (min (v a) (v b)) = Function.update v t (min (v a) (v b))
      by simp [v₁]] at rest
    apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, htest₁, hta], hv⟩
    simp only [astep_jeq htest₁, if_neg ne₁]
    apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, htest₂, htb], hv⟩
    simp only [astep_jeq htest₂, if_neg ne₂]
    apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hbump], hv⟩
    simp only [astep_inc hbump]
    exact rest

end Complexity.Codec
```

```
/-

import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Parse

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# A configuration codec for nondeterministic machines

Configuration-graph algorithms in small space — Savitch's midpoint recursion, the `PATH`
reduction, the inductive counting of Immerman and Szelepcsényi [AB09, §4.1.1, §4.2, §4.3]
— store configurations of a fixed machine `N` on the real input `x` as numbers in
registers. This file fixes that representation: the **code** of a configuration whose work
heads and nonblank work cells lie in the window `[-s, s]` is a word of `O(s + log |x|)` bits,
read as a little-endian number.

## Layout

The code word `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord N s C` is

* `2s + 1` **chunks**, one per work-tape cell `z ∈ [-s, s]` in increasing order, each of the
  fixed width `Complexity.Codec.W N`: a one-hot *header slot* (nonzero only in the leftmost
  chunk, where it names the control state and the output summary), then three bits per work
  tape (`nonblank`, `symbol`, `head here`), then a constant `1`;
* the input head position in binary, little-endian, padded to the fixed width
  `|bits (|x| + 1)|`;
* a final `1`, so that the word is the binary word of its value.

Fixed widths make field extraction position arithmetic, and the cell-major order makes one
machine step a *local* relation between neighbouring chunks (the checks of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Checks`). The code records exactly the
configuration-graph vertex `Turing.NDTM.coreSum` (state, input position, windowed work tapes,
work heads, output summary), so it is injective on window-bounded configurations up to that
vertex, and that is all the graph algorithms need.

This codec is configuration-graph infrastructure, not a result of [AB09]; its conventions
(the window `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` of radius `s`, the output summary) are those of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.Codec.CellV`, `Complexity.Codec.encChunk` — cell values and their chunks.
* `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord`, `Complexity.Codec.cfgCode` — the code word and the code.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeCfg` — the decoder.

## Main results

* `Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode` — the binary word of the code is the code word.
* `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_congr` — the code depends only on the vertex `coreSum`.
* `Complexity.Codec.coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq` — on window-bounded configurations the code
  determines the vertex.
* `Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord`, `Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt` — the code has at most
  `codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)` bits.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeCfg_cfgCode` — decoding a code recovers the vertex.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1: configurations and configuration graphs.)
-/

namespace Complexity.Codec

open Turing LogProg

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool)

/-! ## Words -/

/-- The index of an output summary. -/
def sumIdx : OutSummary → Fin 3
  | .empty => 0
  | .accept => 1
  | .dead => 2

/-- Distinct summaries have distinct indices. -/
lemma sumIdx_injective : Function.Injective sumIdx := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [sumIdx]

/-- The header datum of a configuration: its control state and output-summary index. -/
abbrev Hd := Option N.State × Fin 3

/-- A cell value: the header (present only in the leftmost cell) and, per work tape, the
symbol in the cell and whether the head is on it. -/
abbrev CellV := Option (Hd N) × (Fin N.k → Option Bool × Bool)

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- Cell values have decidable equality. -/
instance CellV.instDecidableEq : DecidableEq (CellV N) := inferInstance

/-- The width of the header slot: the number of header data. -/
def hH : ℕ := Fintype.card (Hd N)

/-- The width of a chunk: header slot, three bits per work tape, a final `1`. -/
def W : ℕ := hH N + 3 * N.k + 1

/-- The chunk width: the header slot, three bits per work tape, and the closing `1`. -/
lemma W_eq : W N = hH N + 3 * N.k + 1 := rfl

/-- The position of a header datum in the one-hot header slot. -/
noncomputable def hdNum (h : Hd N) : ℕ := (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N) h).val

/-- Header positions lie in the slot. -/
lemma hdNum_lt (h : Hd N) : hdNum N h < hH N := (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N) h).isLt

/-- Distinct header data have distinct positions. -/
lemma hdNum_injective : Function.Injective (hdNum N) := by
  intro a b h
  exact (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N)).injective (Fin.ext h)

/-- Bit `t` of the chunk of a cell value: the one-hot header slot, then per tape `nonblank`,
`symbol`, `head here`, then `1`. -/
noncomputable def chunkBit (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) : Bool :=
  if t < hH N then decide (cv.1.map (hdNum N) = some t)
  else if h : (t - hH N) / 3 < N.k then
    if (t - hH N) % 3 = 0 then (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).1.isSome
    else if (t - hH N) % 3 = 1 then (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).1.getD false
    else (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).2
  else true

/-- The chunk of a cell value. -/
noncomputable def encChunk (cv : CellV N) : List Bool :=
  List.ofFn fun t : Fin (W N) => chunkBit N cv t

/-- Chunks have the fixed width `W N`. -/
@[simp] lemma length_encChunk (cv : CellV N) : (encChunk N cv).length = W N := by
  simp only [encChunk, List.length_ofFn]

/-- Bits of a chunk below its width are `chunkBit`. -/
lemma getD_encChunk (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) (ht : t < W N) :
    (encChunk N cv).getD t false = chunkBit N cv t := by
  simp only [encChunk, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_ofFn, ht, dite_true,
    Option.getD_some]

/-- The header-slot bits of a chunk. -/
lemma chunkBit_slot (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) (ht : t < hH N) :
    chunkBit N cv t = decide (cv.1.map (hdNum N) = some t) := by
  simp [chunkBit, ht]

/-- The three bits of tape `i` in a chunk. -/
lemma chunkBit_tape (cv : CellV N) (i : Fin N.k) (r : ℕ) (hr : r < 3) :
    chunkBit N cv (hH N + 3 * i + r) =
      if r = 0 then (cv.2 i).1.isSome else if r = 1 then (cv.2 i).1.getD false
      else (cv.2 i).2 := by
  have e1 : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3 = i := by omega
  have e2 : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) % 3 = r := by omega
  have hi : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3 < N.k := by rw [e1]; exact i.isLt
  simp only [chunkBit, show ¬ hH N + 3 * i + r < hH N by omega, ↓reduceIte, dif_pos hi, e2]
  have : (⟨(hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3, hi⟩ : Fin N.k) = i := Fin.ext e1
  rw [this]

/-- **Chunks are injective**: a cell value is determined by its chunk.

**Proof sketch.** Compare the chunks bit by bit (`getD_encChunk`): the one-hot header slot
determines the header (positions are injective, `hdNum_injective`), and the three bits of each
tape determine the optional symbol and the head flag (`chunkBit_tape`). -/
theorem encChunk_injective : Function.Injective (encChunk N) := by
  intro a b h
  have hb : ∀ t < W N, chunkBit N a t = chunkBit N b t := by
    intro t ht
    rw [← getD_encChunk N a t ht, ← getD_encChunk N b t ht, h]
  obtain ⟨a1, a2⟩ := a
  obtain ⟨b1, b2⟩ := b
  have slot : a1 = b1 := by
    have key : ∀ (u v : Option (Hd N)), (∀ t < hH N, decide (u.map (hdNum N) = some t) =
        decide (v.map (hdNum N) = some t)) → ∀ h, u = some h → v = some h := by
      intro u v hu h hh
      have := hu (hdNum N h) (hdNum_lt N h)
      subst hh
      simp only [Option.map_some, decide_true] at this
      cases v with
      | none => simp at this
      | some g =>
        simp at this
        rw [hdNum_injective N this]
    have hs : ∀ t < hH N, decide (a1.map (hdNum N) = some t) =
        decide (b1.map (hdNum N) = some t) := by
      intro t ht
      have := hb t (by simp only [W]; omega)
      rwa [chunkBit_slot N _ t ht, chunkBit_slot N _ t ht] at this
    cases a1 with
    | some hd => exact (key _ _ hs hd rfl).symm
    | none =>
      cases b1 with
      | none => rfl
      | some g => exact absurd (key _ _ (fun t ht => (hs t ht).symm) g rfl) (by simp)
  subst slot
  congr 1
  funext i
  have bit (r : ℕ) (hr : r < 3) := hb (hH N + 3 * i + r) (by simp only [W]; omega)
  have e0 := bit 0 (by omega)
  have e1 := bit 1 (by omega)
  have e2 := bit 2 (by omega)
  simp only [chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (0 : ℕ) < 3),
    chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (1 : ℕ) < 3),
    chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (2 : ℕ) < 3)] at e0 e1 e2
  simp only [↓reduceIte, one_ne_zero, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, OfNat.ofNat_ne_one] at e0 e1 e2
  revert e0 e1 e2
  obtain ⟨o, hh⟩ := a2 i
  obtain ⟨o', hh'⟩ := b2 i
  intro e0 e1 e2
  simp only at e0 e1 e2
  subst e2
  congr 1
  cases o <;> cases o' <;> simp_all

/-- Concatenated fixed-width blocks: block `j` is recovered by dropping `W · j` letters and
taking `W`. -/
lemma take_drop_flatten {α : Type} (L : List (List α)) (w : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ b ∈ L, b.length = w) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < L.length) :
    ((L.flatten).drop (w * j)).take w = L[j] := by
  induction L generalizing j with
  | nil => simp at hj
  | cons b L ih =>
    have hb := hL b (by simp)
    cases j with
    | zero => simp [← hb]
    | succ j =>
      simp only [List.flatten_cons, List.getElem_cons_succ]
      rw [show w * (j + 1) = b.length + w * j by rw [hb]; ring, ← List.drop_drop,
        List.drop_left]
      exact ih (fun c hc => hL c (by simp [hc])) j (by simpa using hj)

/-- Concatenated blocks of width `w` have length `w` times their number. -/
lemma length_flatten_const {α : Type} (L : List (List α)) (w : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ b ∈ L, b.length = w) : (L.flatten).length = w * L.length := by
  induction L with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b L ih =>
    simp only [List.flatten_cons, List.length_append, List.length_cons,
      hL b (by simp), ih (fun c hc => hL c (by simp [hc]))]
    ring

/-- The word of `m` chunks with cell values `f 0, …, f (m - 1)`. -/
noncomputable def chunksWord (f : ℕ → CellV N) (m : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j)).flatten

/-- A chunk word has `W N` letters per chunk. -/
lemma length_chunksWord (f : ℕ → CellV N) (m : ℕ) :
    (chunksWord N f m).length = W N * m := by
  rw [chunksWord, length_flatten_const _ (W N) (by simp)]
  simp

/-- Equal chunk words have equal cell values. -/
lemma chunksWord_inj {f g : ℕ → CellV N} {m : ℕ} (h : chunksWord N f m = chunksWord N g m)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j < m) : f j = g j := by
  have e1 := take_drop_flatten (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j)) (W N)
    (by simp) j (by simpa using hj)
  have e2 := take_drop_flatten (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (g j)) (W N)
    (by simp) j (by simpa using hj)
  have e : (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j))[j]'(by simpa using hj) =
      (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (g j))[j]'(by simpa using hj) := by
    rw [← e1, ← e2]
    exact congrArg (fun w => (w.drop (W N * j)).take (W N)) h
  simp only [List.getElem_ofFn] at e
  exact encChunk_injective N e

/-! ## The code of a configuration -/

variable {N} {x : List Bool}

/-- The cell value of cell `j` (work position `j - s`) of a configuration: the header in the
leftmost cell, then per tape the symbol at `j - s` and whether the head is there. -/
def cellOf (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (j : ℕ) : CellV N :=
  (if j = 0 then some (C.state, sumIdx (outSummary C.output)) else none,
    fun i => (C.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s), decide (C.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s)))

/-- The head flag of tape `i` in cell `j`: whether the head of tape `i` is at work position
`j - s`. -/
lemma cellOf_head (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (j : ℕ) (i : Fin N.k) :
    ((cellOf s C j).2 i).2 = decide (C.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s) := rfl

/-- The width of the input-position field on inputs of length `n`: `|bits (n + 1)|`. -/
def wP (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length

/-- The position-field width is the binary length of `n + 1`. -/
lemma wP_eq (n : ℕ) : wP n = (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length := rfl

/-- The binary word of `v` padded with `0`s to width `w`. -/
def padBits (w v : ℕ) : List Bool := Nat.bits v ++ List.replicate (w - (Nat.bits v).length) false

/-- **The code word** of a configuration at window radius `s`: the `2s + 1` cell chunks, the
padded input position, and a final `1`. -/
noncomputable def cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : List Bool :=
  chunksWord N (cellOf s C) (2 * s + 1) ++ padBits (wP x.length) C.inputPos.val ++ [true]

/-- **The code** of a configuration at window radius `s`: the value of its code word. -/
noncomputable def cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : ℕ := bitsVal (cfgWord s C)

/-- The value of a word does not see trailing `0`s. -/
lemma bitsVal_append_replicate (w : List Bool) (z : ℕ) :
    bitsVal (w ++ List.replicate z false) = bitsVal w := by
  induction w with
  | nil =>
    induction z with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ z ih => simp [List.replicate_succ, bitsVal] at ih ⊢; exact ih
  | cons b w ih => simp [bitsVal, ih]

/-- Every word is the binary word of its value followed by `0`s.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the word: a leading letter `b` contributes `b + 2 v`; the
binary word of that value is `b` followed by that of `v`, unless both vanish, when the word
is all `0`s. -/
lemma eq_bits_append_replicate (w : List Bool) :
    w = Nat.bits (bitsVal w) ++
      List.replicate (w.length - (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length) false := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal, Nat.zero_bits]
  | cons b w ih =>
    have hl : (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length ≤ w.length := by
      have := congrArg List.length ih
      simp only [List.length_append, List.length_replicate] at this
      omega
    simp only [bitsVal, List.length_cons]
    rw [show b.toNat + 2 * bitsVal w = 2 * bitsVal w + b.toNat by ring]
    by_cases hz : bitsVal w = 0 ∧ b = false
    · obtain ⟨h0, rfl⟩ := hz
      rw [h0] at ih ⊢
      simp only [Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil, Nat.sub_zero, List.nil_append] at ih ⊢
      simp only [Bool.toNat_false, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero, Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil,
        Nat.sub_zero, List.nil_append, List.replicate_succ]
      rw [← ih]
    · rw [bits_two_mul_add _ _ (fun h0 => by
          cases b
          · exact absurd ⟨h0, rfl⟩ hz
          · rfl)]
      simp only [List.length_cons, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, true_and]
      rw [show w.length + 1 - ((Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length + 1) =
        w.length - (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length by omega]
      exact ih

/-- A padded word has the padding width when the value fits. -/
lemma length_padBits {w v : ℕ} (h : (Nat.bits v).length ≤ w) : (padBits w v).length = w := by
  simp [padBits]; omega

/-- The value of a padded word. -/
@[simp] lemma bitsVal_padBits (w v : ℕ) : bitsVal (padBits w v) = v := by
  rw [padBits, bitsVal_append_replicate, bitsVal_bits]

/-- A word of length `w` is the padding of its value to width `w`. -/
lemma eq_padBits (p : List Bool) : p = padBits p.length (bitsVal p) := by
  conv_lhs => rw [eq_bits_append_replicate p]
  rfl

/-- Input positions fit their field. -/
lemma length_bits_pos_le (v n : ℕ) (hv : v ≤ n + 1) : (Nat.bits v).length ≤ wP n :=
  length_bits_mono hv

/-- The number of letters of the code word. -/
lemma length_cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    (cfgWord s C).length = W N * (2 * s + 1) + wP x.length + 1 := by
  have := C.inputPos.isLt
  simp only [cfgWord, List.length_append, length_chunksWord, List.length_singleton]
  rw [length_padBits (length_bits_pos_le _ _ (by omega))]

/-- The code word ends with `1`, so it is the binary word of its value. -/
lemma canon_cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : Canon (cfgWord s C) := by
  intro h
  simp [cfgWord]

/-- **The binary word of the code is the code word.** -/
theorem bits_cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    Nat.bits (cfgCode s C) = cfgWord s C :=
  (canon_eq_bits _ (canon_cfgWord s C)).symm

/-- The cell values depend only on the configuration-graph vertex. -/
lemma cellOf_congr {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x} (h : NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D) :
    cellOf s C = cellOf s D := by
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨hs, -, hw, hp⟩, ho⟩ := h
  funext j
  simp only [cellOf, hs, hw, hp, ho]

/-- **The code depends only on the configuration-graph vertex** `coreSum`. -/
theorem cfgWord_congr {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x}
    (h : NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D) : cfgWord s C = cfgWord s D := by
  have hi : C.inputPos = D.inputPos := by
    simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    exact h.1.2.1
  simp only [cfgWord, cellOf_congr h, hi]

/-- **On window-bounded configurations the code determines the vertex**: equal code words
give equal `coreSum`.

**Proof sketch.** The two words have the same length, so their chunk prefixes, position
fields and final letters align. Equal chunks give equal cell values (`chunksWord_inj`):
the leftmost cell yields the state and the summary (`sumIdx` is injective, and summaries
determine the vertex component), every cell yields the tape symbols and head flags at its
position, and outside `[-s, s]` both tapes are blank and no head lies there (window
hypotheses). Equal position fields have equal values (`bitsVal_padBits`). -/
theorem coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x}
    (hC : Cfg.InWindow s C) (hD : Cfg.InWindow s D) (h : cfgWord s C = cfgWord s D) :
    NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D := by
  have hlen : (chunksWord N (cellOf s C) (2 * s + 1)).length =
      (chunksWord N (cellOf s D) (2 * s + 1)).length := by simp [length_chunksWord]
  simp only [cfgWord, List.append_assoc] at h
  obtain ⟨hc, hrest⟩ := List.append_inj h hlen
  have hpos := congrArg bitsVal (List.append_inj_left' hrest rfl)
  simp only [bitsVal_padBits] at hpos
  have cell := chunksWord_inj N hc
  have c0 := cell 0 (by omega)
  simp only [cellOf, ↓reduceIte, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.some.injEq] at c0
  obtain ⟨⟨hst, hsum⟩, -⟩ := c0
  have hsum' := sumIdx_injective hsum
  have tape : ∀ i (z : ℤ), |z| ≤ s → C.workTapes i z = D.workTapes i z ∧
      (C.workTapePos i = z ↔ D.workTapePos i = z) := by
    intro i z hz
    have := cell (z + s).toNat (by rw [abs_le] at hz; omega)
    simp only [cellOf, Prod.mk.injEq] at this
    have e := congrFun this.2 i
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, decide_eq_decide] at e
    have hz' : (((z + s).toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) - s = z := by rw [abs_le] at hz; omega
    rwa [hz'] at e
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq]
  refine ⟨⟨hst, Fin.ext hpos, ?_, ?_⟩, hsum'⟩
  · funext i z
    by_cases hz : |z| ≤ s
    · exact (tape i z hz).1
    · have h1 : C.workTapes i z = none := hC.2 i z (not_le.mp hz)
      have h2 : D.workTapes i z = none := hD.2 i z (not_le.mp hz)
      rw [h1, h2]
  · funext i
    exact ((tape i _ (hC.1 i)).2.mp rfl).symm

/-- The constant of the code length: `2 W + 2`. -/
def codeK (N : FinNDTM Bool) : ℕ := 2 * W N + 2

/-- **The code is short**: the code word has at most `codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)`
letters, so the code is below `2 ^ (codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1))`. The input field
has `|bits (|x| + 1)| ≤ logSpace |x| + 1` letters.

**Proof sketch.** Count `W (2s + 1)` chunk letters, the position field, and the final `1`;
`|bits (n + 1)| ≤ ⌊log₂ (n + 1)⌋ + 1 ≤ logSpace n + 1` and `W ≥ 1`. -/
theorem length_cfgWord_le (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    (cfgWord s C).length ≤ codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) := by
  rw [length_cfgWord]
  have h1 : wP x.length ≤ logSpace x.length + 1 := by
    have e := length_bits_le_log (x.length + 1)
    have e2 : Nat.log 2 (x.length + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 x.length + 1 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos x.length with h | h
      · rw [h]; simp
      · have := Nat.log_mul_base (b := 2) (n := x.length) (by norm_num) (by omega)
        have := Nat.log_mono_right (b := 2) (show x.length + 1 ≤ x.length * 2 by omega)
        omega
    simp only [wP, logSpace]; omega
  have hW : 1 ≤ W N := by simp [W]
  simp only [codeK]
  have e1 : W N * (2 * s + 1) = 2 * (W N * s) + W N := by ring
  have e2 : (2 * W N + 2) * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) =
      2 * (W N * s) + 2 * (W N * logSpace x.length) + 2 * W N + 2 * s +
        2 * logSpace x.length + 2 := by ring
  rw [e1, e2]
  omega

/-- A word of `L` letters has value below `2 ^ L`. -/
lemma bitsVal_lt_two_pow (w : List Bool) : bitsVal w < 2 ^ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal]
  | cons b w ih =>
    simp only [bitsVal, List.length_cons, pow_succ]
    cases b <;> simp <;> omega

/-- **The code is below `2 ^ (codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1))`.** -/
theorem cfgCode_lt (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    cfgCode s C < 2 ^ (codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1)) :=
  (bitsVal_lt_two_pow _).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_cfgWord_le s C))

/-! ## Decoding -/

open Classical in
/-- **The decoder**: a window-bounded configuration with code `c` at radius `s`, if any
(chosen; it is determined up to the configuration-graph vertex,
`decodeCfg_cfgCode`). -/
noncomputable def decodeCfg (x : List Bool) (s c : ℕ) : Option (Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :=
  if h : ∃ C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s C ∧ cfgCode s C = c then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- **Decoding a code recovers the vertex**: the decoder succeeds on the code of a
window-bounded configuration, with a window-bounded result of the same code and vertex.

**Proof sketch.** The chosen configuration has the same code, hence the same code word
(`bits_cfgCode`), hence the same vertex (`coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq`). -/
theorem decodeCfg_cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (hC : Cfg.InWindow s C) :
    ∃ D, decodeCfg x s (cfgCode s C) = some D ∧ Cfg.InWindow s D ∧ cfgCode s D = cfgCode s C ∧
      NDTM.coreSum D = NDTM.coreSum C := by
  classical
  have h : ∃ D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s D ∧ cfgCode s D = cfgCode s C :=
    ⟨C, hC, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨Classical.choose h, by simp [decodeCfg, h], (Classical.choose_spec h).1,
    (Classical.choose_spec h).2, ?_⟩
  apply coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq (Classical.choose_spec h).1 hC
  rw [← bits_cfgCode, ← bits_cfgCode, (Classical.choose_spec h).2]

/-- The decoder fails exactly on numbers that are not codes. -/
theorem decodeCfg_eq_none (s c : ℕ) :
    decodeCfg (N := N) x s c = none ↔
      ¬ ∃ C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s C ∧ cfgCode s C = c := by
  classical
  unfold decodeCfg
  split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]

end Complexity.Codec
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/ConfigCount.lean =====

```
/-
```
