The bank answers the simulator's queries `⟨y, bits i⟩` about the virtual input `epadVirt y`.
On an input `z` it counts `|z|`, parses `z = ⟨y, w⟩`, checks that the index word `w` is
canonical and no wider than `|y|`, decodes `i = bitsVal w`, runs the validity block on `y` at
stride `2` (`y`'s letters are `z`'s doubled first field), and then seeks `i` below `|a|` with
stride `4` (letter `i` of `a` is letter `4i` of `z`): mode `false` answers whether it is found,
mode `true` reads the letter found. Registers `9` … `17`: `|z|`, the pointer, the tail base,
the cap, `i`, the decoder's scratch, and the seek's pointer, limit and index. -/

/-- The bank's labels around the validity block. -/
private inductive EPadBX where
  | lscan | linc
  | zscan | zfirst | ztest (b : Bool) | zread (b : Bool) | zadv (k : Fin 4)
  | c1T | c1B | c2T | c2B | dd1 | dd2 | c3T | c3B | hcap
  | ttest (b : Bool) | tcheck | tread | thalve (b : Bool) | tadv (b : Bool)
  | c4T | c4B
  | dtest | ddown | dread | dcopy (b : Bool) | dbump (b : Bool) | dclear (b : Bool)
  | dscale (b : Bool) | dtake (b : Bool) | dinc (b : Bool) (second : Bool) | dadd (b : Bool)
  | q1T | q1B | q1d | qsT | qsD | qsI (i : Fin 4)
  | seek | probe | bump | sadv (i : Fin 4) | hit
  | yes | no

/-- Every bank label, listed. -/
private def epadBXAll : List EPadBX :=
  [.lscan, .linc, .zscan, .zfirst, .ztest false, .ztest true, .zread false, .zread true] ++
  (List.finRange 4).map .zadv ++
  [.c1T, .c1B, .c2T, .c2B, .dd1, .dd2, .c3T, .c3B, .hcap, .ttest false, .ttest true, .tcheck,
    .tread, .thalve false, .thalve true, .tadv false, .tadv true, .c4T, .c4B, .dtest, .ddown,
    .dread] ++
  ([false, true].flatMap fun b => [.dcopy b, .dbump b, .dclear b, .dscale b, .dtake b,
    .dinc b false, .dinc b true, .dadd b]) ++
  [.q1T, .q1B, .q1d, .qsT, .qsD] ++ (List.finRange 4).map .qsI ++
  [.seek, .probe, .bump] ++ (List.finRange 4).map .sadv ++ [.hit, .yes, .no]

/-- The bank's labels form a finite type (a local instance of the proofs). -/
private noncomputable def epadBXFintype : Fintype EPadBX := by
  classical
  refine Fintype.ofList epadBXAll (fun l => ?_)
  cases l with
  | dcopy b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | dbump b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | dclear b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | dscale b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | dtake b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | dinc b c => cases b <;> cases c <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | dadd b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | ztest b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | zread b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | ttest b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | thalve b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | tadv b => cases b <;> simp [epadBXAll]
  | _ => simp [epadBXAll]

/-- The targets of the outer pair scan's advances. -/
private def epadZEnd (k : Fin 4) : EPadBX :=
  if k = 0 then .ztest false else if k = 1 then .ztest true else if k = 2 then .zscan else .c1T

/-- **The bank** in mode `mode`, as an abstract register machine. -/
private def epadBA (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) : ARM 18 2 (EPadVL C d ⊕ EPadBX)
  | .inl l => epadValCode true C d Sum.inl (.inr .q1T) (.inr .no) l
  | .inr .lscan => .call 1 .whole [9] (.inr .linc) (.inr .zscan)
  | .inr .linc => .inc 9 (.inr .lscan)
  | .inr .zscan => .jeq 10 9 (.inr .no) (.inr .zfirst)
  | .inr .zfirst => .call 0 .whole [10] (.inr (.zadv 1)) (.inr (.zadv 0))
  | .inr (.ztest b) => .jeq 10 9 (.inr .no) (.inr (.zread b))
  | .inr (.zread b) => .call 0 .whole [10] (if b then .inr (.zadv 2) else .inr (.zadv 3))
      (if b then .inr .no else .inr (.zadv 2))
  | .inr (.zadv k) => .inc 10 (.inr (epadZEnd k))
  | .inr .c1T => .jeq 11 10 (.inr .c2T) (.inr .c1B)
  | .inr .c1B => .inc 11 (.inr .c1T)
  | .inr .c2T => .jeq 1 10 (.inr .dd1) (.inr .c2B)
  | .inr .c2B => .inc 1 (.inr .c2T)
  | .inr .dd1 => .dec 1 (.inr .dd2)
  | .inr .dd2 => .dec 1 (.inr .c3T)
  | .inr .c3T => .jeq 12 1 (.inr .hcap) (.inr .c3B)
  | .inr .c3B => .inc 12 (.inr .c3T)
  | .inr .hcap => .half 12 (.inr (.ttest true))
  | .inr (.ttest b) => .jeq 10 9 (if b then .inr .c4T else .inr .no) (.inr .tcheck)
  | .inr .tcheck => .jz 12 (.inr .no) (.inr .tread)
  | .inr .tread => .call 0 .whole [10] (.inr (.thalve true)) (.inr (.thalve false))
  | .inr (.thalve b) => .half 12 (.inr (.tadv b))
  | .inr (.tadv b) => .inc 10 (.inr (.ttest b))
  | .inr .c4T => .jeq 10 9 (.inr .dtest) (.inr .c4B)
  | .inr .c4B => .inc 10 (.inr .c4T)
  | .inr .dtest => .jeq 10 11 (.inl .scan) (.inr .ddown)
  | .inr .ddown => .dec 10 (.inr .dread)
  | .inr .dread => .call 0 .whole [10] (.inr (.dcopy true)) (.inr (.dcopy false))
  | .inr (.dcopy b) => .jeq 14 13 (.inr (.dclear b)) (.inr (.dbump b))
  | .inr (.dbump b) => .inc 14 (.inr (.dcopy b))
  | .inr (.dclear b) => .clr 13 (.inr (.dscale b))
  | .inr (.dscale b) => .jz 14 (.inr (.dadd b)) (.inr (.dtake b))
  | .inr (.dtake b) => .dec 14 (.inr (.dinc b false))
  | .inr (.dinc b false) => .inc 13 (.inr (.dinc b true))
  | .inr (.dinc b true) => .inc 13 (.inr (.dscale b))
  | .inr (.dadd b) => if b then .inc 13 (.inr .dtest) else .jz 14 (.inr .dtest) (.inr .dtest)
  | .inr .q1T => .jeq 17 2 (.inr .q1d) (.inr .q1B)
  | .inr .q1B => .inc 17 (.inr .q1T)
  | .inr .q1d => .dec 17 (.inr .qsT)
  | .inr .qsT => .jz 17 (.inr .seek) (.inr .qsD)
  | .inr .qsD => .dec 17 (.inr (.qsI 0))
  | .inr (.qsI i) => .inc 16 (if i = 3 then .inr .qsT else .inr (.qsI (i + 1)))
  | .inr .seek => .jeq 15 16 (.inr .no) (.inr .probe)
  | .inr .probe => .jeq 17 13 (.inr .hit) (.inr .bump)
  | .inr .bump => .inc 17 (.inr (.sadv 0))
  | .inr (.sadv i) => .inc 15 (if i = 3 then .inr .seek else .inr (.sadv (i + 1)))
  | .inr .hit => if mode then .call 0 .whole [15] (.inr .yes) (.inr .no) else .ret true
  | .inr .yes => .ret true
  | .inr .no => .ret false

/-- **The bank's last phase.** From `q1T`, with `na + 1` in register `2`, the index `i` in
register `13` and the seek registers `15`, `16`, `17` clear, the bank answers: in mode `false`
whether `i < na`; in mode `true` letter `4i` of the input if `i < na`, and `0` otherwise.

**Proof sketch.** `registerCopy_loop` and one decrement load `na` into register `17`;
`registerScale_loop` at factor `4` moves `4 na` into the seek limit `16`; `indexedSeek_loop` at
stride `4` hits exactly when `i < na`, with its pointer at `4i`. -/
private theorem epad_bank_post (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (z : List Bool) (B na i : ℕ)
    (v : Fin 18 → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B) (h2 : v 2 = na + 1) (h13 : v 13 = i)
    (h15 : v 15 = 0) (h16 : v 16 = 0) (h17 : v 17 = 0) (hB : 4 * na + 1 ≤ B) :
    AHalt (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .q1T), v, none)
      (if i < na then (if mode then z.getD (4 * i) false else true) else false) := by
  -- `17 := na + 1`, then `na`
  have hc1 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 17 2 (by decide) (.inr .q1T)
    (.inr .q1B) (.inr .q1d) rfl rfl B v hv (by rw [h17]; exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update v 17 (v 2) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₁] at hc1
  have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₁]; exact register_update_le v 17 B _ hv (hv 2)
  obtain ⟨v₂, hv₂⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update v₁ 17 na := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have b₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₂]; exact register_update_le v₁ 17 B _ b₁ (by omega)
  have hd : AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .q1d), v₁, none)
      (some (.inr .qsT), v₂, none) := by
    have hc : epadBA C d mode (.inr .q1d) = .dec 17 (.inr .qsT) := rfl
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc trivial, b₁⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_dec hc, hv₂, hv₁, Function.update_self, h2, Nat.add_sub_cancel,
      Function.update_idem]
    exact AReach.refl _
  -- `16 += 4 · 17`, `17 := 0`
  have hsc := registerScale_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 17 16 (by decide) (.inr .qsT)
    (.inr .qsD) (.inr .seek) (fun i => if h : i < 4 then .inr (.qsI ⟨i, h⟩) else .inr .qsT) 4
    rfl rfl (fun i hi => by
      obtain rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 ∨ i = 2 ∨ i = 3 := by omega
      all_goals rfl) rfl B v₂ b₂ (by
        rw [hv₂, Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₁,
          Function.update_of_ne (by decide), h16]
        omega)
  obtain ⟨v₃, hv₃⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (Function.update v₂ 17 0) 16
      (v₂ 16 + 4 * v₂ 17) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₃] at hsc
  have h₃ : ∀ r, v₃ r = if r = 16 then 4 * na else if r = 17 then 0 else v r := by
    intro r
    rw [hv₃, hv₂, hv₁]
    simp only [Function.update_apply, Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h16]
    split_ifs <;> subst_vars <;> simp_all
  have b₃ : ∀ r, v₃ r ≤ B := by
    intro r; rw [h₃]; split_ifs
    · omega
    · exact Nat.zero_le _
    · exact hv r
  -- the seek
  have hseek := indexedSeek_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 15 16 17 13 (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.inr .seek) (.inr .probe) (.inr .bump)
    (.inr .hit) (.inr .no) (fun i => if h : i < 4 then .inr (.sadv ⟨i, h⟩) else .inr .seek) 4 B
    (by omega) rfl rfl rfl (fun i hi => by
      obtain rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 ∨ i = 2 ∨ i = 3 := by omega
      all_goals rfl) rfl na v₃ b₃
    (by rw [h₃, h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h15]; omega)
    (by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; omega)
    (by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; exact Nat.zero_le _)
  have h313 : v₃ 13 = i := by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h13]
  have h317 : v₃ 17 = 0 := by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  have h315 : v₃ 15 = 0 := by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h15]
  rw [h313, h317, Nat.zero_add] at hseek
  refine hc1.halt (hd.halt (hsc.halt ?_))
  by_cases hi : i < na
  · rw [if_pos hi] at hseek ⊢
    obtain ⟨v₄, hv₄⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (Function.update v₃ 15 (v₃ 15 + 4 * (i - 0)))
        17 i := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    rw [← hv₄] at hseek
    have b₄ : ∀ r, v₄ r ≤ B := by
      rw [hv₄]
      refine register_update_le _ 17 B _ (register_update_le _ 15 B _ b₃ ?_) (by omega)
      rw [h315]; omega
    have h415 : v₄ 15 = 4 * i := by
      rw [hv₄, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), Function.update_self, h315]; omega
    refine hseek.halt ?_
    cases mode with
    | false =>
      exact AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d false (.inr .hit) = .ret true from rfl)
        trivial, b₄⟩
    | true =>
      have hc : epadBA C d true (.inr .hit) = .call 0 .whole [15] (.inr .yes) (.inr .no) := rfl
      refine AHalt.step ⟨epad_preS hc (List.nodup_singleton _), b₄⟩ ?_
      rw [astep_call hc, vword_whole₁, h415]
      have ho : epadOr 0 (pairEncode z (Nat.bits (4 * i))) = z.getD (4 * i) false :=
        (epadIn_answer z (4 * i)).1
      rw [ho]
      cases hb : z.getD (4 * i) false
      · exact AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d true (.inr .no) = .ret false from rfl)
          trivial, b₄⟩
      · exact AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d true (.inr .yes) = .ret true from rfl)
          trivial, b₄⟩
  · rw [if_neg hi] at hseek ⊢
    obtain ⟨v₄, hv₄⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (Function.update v₃ 15 (v₃ 16)) 17 na :=
      ⟨_, rfl⟩
    rw [← hv₄] at hseek
    have b₄ : ∀ r, v₄ r ≤ B := by
      rw [hv₄]
      exact register_update_le _ 17 B _ (register_update_le _ 15 B _ b₃ (b₃ 16)) (by omega)
    exact hseek.halt (AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS
      (show epadBA C d mode (.inr .no) = .ret false from rfl) trivial, b₄⟩)

/-- A number of `|bits n|` binary digits is below `2 n + 2`: `2 ^ |bits n| ≤ 2 n + 1`. -/
private lemma epad_two_pow_bits (n : ℕ) : 2 ^ (Nat.bits n).length ≤ 2 * n + 1 := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · simp [Nat.zero_bits]
  · have h1 := length_bits_le_log n
    have h2 : 2 ^ Nat.log 2 n ≤ n := Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 (by omega)
    calc 2 ^ (Nat.bits n).length ≤ 2 ^ (Nat.log 2 n + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) h1
      _ = 2 * 2 ^ Nat.log 2 n := by rw [pow_succ]; ring
      _ ≤ 2 * n + 1 := by omega

/-- **The bank's first phase.** From the start, the bank counts `|z|` and parses
`z = ⟨y, w⟩`; it rejects a word that is not a pair, or whose index word `w` is not canonical
or wider than `|y|`; otherwise it decodes `i = bitsVal w` into register `13` and enters the
validity block with its pointer `0`, its limit `2 |y|` and its working registers clear, the
seek registers `15`–`17` clear, all registers at most `B`.

**Proof sketch.** `inputLength_loop`; `alignedPair_loop` at stride `1` on `z`; three
`registerCopy_loop`s, two decrements and a halving set the tail base `2|y| + 2`, the block's
limit `2|y|` and the cap `|y|`; `canonicalTail_loop` checks the index word; one more copy moves
the pointer to the end, and `boundedDecode_loop` decodes the index (its values stay below
`2 ^ |bits |y||` by `Codec.bitsVal_lt_two_pow`). -/
private theorem epad_bank_pre (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (z : List Bool) (B : ℕ)
    (hB : 2 * z.length + 1 ≤ B) :
    (pairDecode z = none → ∃ v, (∀ r, v r ≤ B) ∧
      AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B)
        (some (.inr .lscan), fun _ => 0, none) (some (.inr .no), v, none)) ∧
    (∀ y w, pairDecode z = some (y, w) →
      (¬ (w.getLastD true = true ∧ w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length) → ∃ v, (∀ r, v r ≤ B) ∧
        AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
          (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B)
          (some (.inr .lscan), fun _ => 0, none) (some (.inr .no), v, none)) ∧
      (w.getLastD true = true ∧ w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length → ∃ v, (∀ r, v r ≤ B) ∧
        v 0 = 0 ∧ v 1 = 2 * y.length ∧ (∀ r : Fin 18, 2 ≤ r.val → r.val ≤ 8 → v r = 0) ∧
        v 13 = LogProg.bitsVal w ∧ v 15 = 0 ∧ v 16 = 0 ∧ v 17 = 0 ∧
        AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
          (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B)
          (some (.inr .lscan), fun _ => 0, none) (some (.inl .scan), v, none))) := by
  -- the length
  have hlen := inputLength_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 9 1 (.inr .lscan) (.inr .linc)
    (.inr .zscan) rfl rfl (fun n _ => (epadIn_answer z n).2) B (by omega) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₀, hv₀⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (fun _ : Fin 18 => 0) 9 z.length := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₀] at hlen
  have b₀ : ∀ r, v₀ r ≤ B := by
    rw [hv₀]; exact register_update_le _ 9 B _ (fun _ => Nat.zero_le _) (by omega)
  have h₀ : ∀ r : Fin 18, r ≠ 9 → v₀ r = 0 := fun r hr => by
    rw [hv₀, Function.update_of_ne hr]
  have h₀9 : v₀ 9 = z.length := by rw [hv₀, Function.update_self]
  -- the outer pair scan
  have hap := alignedPair_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 9 0 (.inr .zscan) (.inr .zfirst)
    (fun b => .inr (.ztest b)) (fun b => .inr (.zread b)) (.inr .no) (.inr .c1T)
    (fun k i => if i = 0 then .inr (.zadv k) else .inr (epadZEnd k)) 1 B (by omega) (by decide)
    rfl rfl (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun k i hi => by obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
                      rfl)
    ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩ z v₀ b₀ (by rw [h₀9, h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega)
    (fun i _ => by rw [h₀ 10 (by decide), Nat.zero_add, Nat.one_mul]
                   exact (epadIn_answer z i).1)
  refine ⟨fun hd => ?_, fun y w hd => ?_⟩
  · simp only [hd] at hap
    obtain ⟨t, ht, hr⟩ := hap
    exact ⟨_, register_update_le v₀ 10 B _ b₀ (by rw [h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega), hlen.trans hr⟩
  simp only [hd] at hap
  have hz : z = pairEncode y w := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z y w hd
  have hzl : z.length = 2 * y.length + 2 + w.length := by rw [hz, length_pairEncode]
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₀ 10 (v₀ 10 + 1 * (2 * y.length + 2)) :=
    ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₁] at hap
  have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := by
    rw [hv₁]; exact register_update_le v₀ 10 B _ b₀ (by rw [h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega)
  have h₁10 : v₁ 10 = 2 * y.length + 2 := by
    rw [hv₁, Function.update_self, h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega
  -- the tail base, the block's limit and the cap
  have hc1 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 11 10 (by decide) (.inr .c1T)
    (.inr .c1B) (.inr .c2T) rfl rfl B v₁ b₁ (by
      rw [hv₁, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), h₀ 11 (by decide)]; exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₂, hv₂⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₁ 11 (v₁ 10) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₂] at hc1
  have b₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₂]; exact register_update_le v₁ 11 B _ b₁ (b₁ 10)
  have hc2 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 1 10 (by decide) (.inr .c2T)
    (.inr .c2B) (.inr .dd1) rfl rfl B v₂ b₂ (by
      rw [hv₂, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₁, Function.update_of_ne (by decide),
        h₀ 1 (by decide)]
      exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₃, hv₃⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₂ 1 (v₂ 10) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₃] at hc2
  have b₃ : ∀ r, v₃ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₃]; exact register_update_le v₂ 1 B _ b₂ (b₂ 10)
  have h₂10 : v₂ 10 = 2 * y.length + 2 := by
    rw [hv₂, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), h₁10]
  obtain ⟨v₄, hv₄⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₃ 1 (2 * y.length) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have b₄ : ∀ r, v₄ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₄]; exact register_update_le v₃ 1 B _ b₃ (by omega)
  have hdd : AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .dd1), v₃, none)
      (some (.inr .c3T), v₄, none) := by
    have hc : epadBA C d mode (.inr .dd1) = .dec 1 (.inr .dd2) := rfl
    have hc' : epadBA C d mode (.inr .dd2) = .dec 1 (.inr .c3T) := rfl
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc trivial, b₃⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_dec hc]
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc' trivial,
      register_update_le v₃ 1 B _ b₃ ((Nat.sub_le _ _).trans (b₃ 1))⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_dec hc']
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v₃ 1 (v₃ 1 - 1)) 1
        (Function.update v₃ 1 (v₃ 1 - 1) 1 - 1) = v₄ := by
      rw [hv₄, hv₃]
      funext s
      simp only [Function.update_apply]
      split_ifs <;> simp_all
    rw [e]
    exact AReach.refl _
  have hc3 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 12 1 (by decide) (.inr .c3T)
    (.inr .c3B) (.inr .hcap) rfl rfl B v₄ b₄ (by
      rw [hv₄, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₃, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₂,
        Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₁, Function.update_of_ne (by decide),
        h₀ 12 (by decide)]
      exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₅, hv₅⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₄ 12 (v₄ 1) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₅] at hc3
  have b₅ : ∀ r, v₅ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₅]; exact register_update_le v₄ 12 B _ b₄ (b₄ 1)
  obtain ⟨v₆, hv₆⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₅ 12 y.length := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have b₆ : ∀ r, v₆ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₆]; exact register_update_le v₅ 12 B _ b₅ (by omega)
  have hhc : AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .hcap), v₅, none)
      (some (.inr (.ttest true)), v₆, none) := by
    have hc : epadBA C d mode (.inr .hcap) = .half 12 (.inr (.ttest true)) := rfl
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc trivial, b₅⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_half hc]
    have e : Function.update v₅ 12 (v₅ 12 / 2) = v₆ := by
      rw [hv₆, hv₅]
      funext s
      simp only [Function.update_apply]
      split_ifs <;> simp_all
    rw [e]
    exact AReach.refl _
  -- the register file before the tail check
  have h₆ : ∀ r : Fin 18, v₆ r = if r = 1 then 2 * y.length else if r = 9 then z.length
      else if r = 10 then 2 * y.length + 2 else if r = 11 then 2 * y.length + 2
      else if r = 12 then y.length else 0 := by
    intro r
    rw [hv₆, hv₅, hv₄, hv₃, hv₂, hv₁, hv₀]
    simp only [Function.update_apply, Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
    split_ifs <;> simp_all
  -- the tail check
  have hct := canonicalTail_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 9 12 (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) 0 (fun b => .inr (.ttest b)) (.inr .tcheck) (.inr .tread) (.inr .no) (.inr .c4T)
    (fun b => .inr (.thalve b)) (fun b i => if i = 0 then .inr (.tadv b) else .inr (.ttest b))
    1 B (by omega) (fun _ => rfl) rfl rfl (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun b i hi => by obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
                      rfl)
    (fun _ => rfl) w true v₆ b₆ (by rw [h₆, h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; omega)
    (fun i hi => by
      rw [h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, Nat.one_mul]
      rw [(epadIn_answer z _).1, hz, pairEncode_getD_snd])
  obtain ⟨v', b', hp', hfr', hct⟩ := hct
  have h612 : v₆ 12 = y.length := by rw [h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  rw [h612] at hct
  refine ⟨fun hbad => ?_, fun hok => ?_⟩
  · have hno : (if w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length then
        (if w.getLastD true = true then (Sum.inr EPadBX.c4T : EPadVL C d ⊕ EPadBX)
          else .inr .no) else .inr .no) = .inr .no := by
      split_ifs with h1 h2
      · exact absurd ⟨h2, h1⟩ hbad
      · rfl
      · rfl
    rw [hno] at hct
    exact ⟨v', b', hlen.trans (hap.trans (hc1.trans (hc2.trans (hdd.trans (hc3.trans
      (hhc.trans hct))))))⟩
  rw [if_pos hok.2, if_pos hok.1] at hct
  -- the pointer to the end, then the decoder
  have h'9 : v' 9 = z.length := by
    rw [hfr' 9 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  have hc4 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 9 (by decide) (.inr .c4T)
    (.inr .c4B) (.inr .dtest) rfl rfl B v' b' (by
      rw [h'9]; rw [h₆] at hp'; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte] at hp'; exact hp')
  obtain ⟨v₇, hv₇⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v' 10 (v' 9) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₇] at hc4
  have b₇ : ∀ r, v₇ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₇]; exact register_update_le v' 10 B _ b' (b' 9)
  have h₇ : ∀ r : Fin 18, r ≠ 10 → r ≠ 12 → v₇ r = v₆ r := fun r h10 h12 => by
    rw [hv₇, Function.update_of_ne h10, hfr' r h10 h12]
  have hw : w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length := hok.2
  have hval : ∀ i ≤ w.length, LogProg.bitsVal (w.drop i) ≤ B := by
    intro i _
    have h1 := Codec.bitsVal_lt_two_pow (w.drop i)
    have h2 : 2 ^ (w.drop i).length ≤ 2 ^ (Nat.bits y.length).length :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) ((by simp : (w.drop i).length ≤ w.length).trans hw)
    have h3 := epad_two_pow_bits y.length
    omega
  have hdec := boundedDecode_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 11 13 14 (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) 0 (.inr .dtest) (.inr .ddown)
    (.inr .dread) (.inl .scan) (fun b => .inr (.dcopy b)) (fun b => .inr (.dbump b))
    (fun b => .inr (.dclear b)) (fun b => .inr (.dscale b)) (fun b => .inr (.dtake b))
    (fun b => .inr (.dadd b))
    (fun b i => if i = 0 then .inr (.dinc b false) else if i = 1 then .inr (.dinc b true)
      else .inr (.dscale b))
    rfl rfl rfl (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun b i hi => by
      obtain rfl | rfl : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 := by omega
      all_goals rfl)
    (fun _ => rfl) (fun b => by cases b <;> rfl) w B hval w.length le_rfl v₇ b₇
    (by rw [hv₇, Function.update_self, h'9, Function.update_of_ne (by decide),
          hfr' 11 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
        simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; omega)
    (by rw [h₇ 13 (by decide) (by decide), h₆, List.drop_length]
        simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
        rw [← Nat.zero_bits, LogProg.bitsVal_bits])
    (by rw [h₇ 14 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte])
    (fun i hi => by
      rw [h₇ 11 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
      rw [(epadIn_answer z _).1, hz, pairEncode_getD_snd])
  obtain ⟨v'', b'', -, h''13, -, hfr'', hdec⟩ := hdec
  have h'' : ∀ r : Fin 18, r ≠ 10 → r ≠ 12 → r ≠ 13 → r ≠ 14 → v'' r = v₆ r :=
    fun r h10 h12 h13 h14 => by rw [hfr'' r h10 h13 h14, h₇ r h10 h12]
  refine ⟨v'', b'', ?_, ?_, fun r h2 h8 => ?_, h''13, ?_, ?_, ?_, hlen.trans (hap.trans
    (hc1.trans (hc2.trans (hdd.trans (hc3.trans (hhc.trans (hct.trans (hc4.trans hdec))))))))⟩
  · rw [h'' 0 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  · rw [h'' 1 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [↓reduceIte]
  · have hne : ∀ k : Fin 18, 9 ≤ k.val → r ≠ k := fun k hk h => by rw [h] at h8; omega
    have hne1 : r ≠ 1 := fun h => by rw [h] at h2; simp at h2
    rw [h'' r (hne 10 (by decide)) (hne 12 (by decide)) (hne 13 (by decide))
      (hne 14 (by decide)), h₆, if_neg hne1, if_neg (hne 9 (by decide)),
      if_neg (hne 10 (by decide)), if_neg (hne 11 (by decide)), if_neg (hne 12 (by decide))]
  · rw [h'' 15 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  · rw [h'' 16 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  · rw [h'' 17 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]

/-- Letter `4i` of `⟨⟨a, b⟩, w⟩` is letter `i` of `a`, for `i < |a|`. -/
private lemma epad_getD_four (a b w : List Bool) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < a.length) :
    (pairEncode (pairEncode a b) w).getD (4 * i) false = a.getD i false := by
  rw [pairEncode_getD, if_pos (by rw [length_pairEncode]; omega),
    show 4 * i / 2 = 2 * i by omega, pairEncode_getD, if_pos (by omega),
    show 2 * i / 2 = i by omega]

/-- **The bank** (checkpoint 3): both query languages are decided in logarithmic space.

**Proof sketch.** `arm_decides_poly` on `epadBA`: the first phase `epad_bank_pre` parses the
query and decodes its index (rejecting malformed queries), the validity block `epad_val_run`
runs at stride `2` on the first field (rejecting unpadded words), and `epad_bank_post` answers.
Registers stay below `(C + d + 8)(|z| + 1)^{d + 1}`. -/
private theorem epad_Q_mem (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) : epadQ C d mode ∈ LOGSPACE := by
  classical
  letI := epadVLFintype C d
  letI := epadBXFintype
  refine arm_decides_poly (epadBA C d mode) (.inr .lscan) epadIn epadIn_mem (C + d + 8) (d + 1)
    fun z => ?_
  have hB := epad_bound C d z.length
  obtain ⟨hnone, hsome⟩ := epad_bank_pre C d mode z ((C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1))
    (by omega)
  have hno : ∀ v : Fin 18 → ℕ, (∀ r, v r ≤ (C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1)) →
      AHalt (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧
        ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ (C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1)) (some (.inr .no), v, none)
        false := fun v hv =>
    AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d mode (.inr .no) = .ret false from rfl) trivial, hv⟩
  cases hd : pairDecode z with
  | none =>
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hr⟩ := hnone hd
    have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z = false := by
      rw [indicator_eq_decide]; exact decide_eq_false (epad_not_mem_Q hd)
    rw [hans]
    exact hr.halt (hno v hv)
  | some yw =>
    obtain ⟨y, w⟩ := yw
    obtain ⟨hbad, hok⟩ := hsome y w hd
    have hz : z = pairEncode y w := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z y w hd
    have hzl : z.length = 2 * y.length + 2 + w.length := by rw [hz, length_pairEncode]
    by_cases hw : w.getLastD true = true ∧ w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length
    · obtain ⟨v, hv, h0, h1, hzr, h13, h15, h16, h17, hr⟩ := hok hw
      have hpowy : C * (y.length + 1) ^ d ≤ C * (z.length + 1) ^ d :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) _)
      obtain ⟨v', hfr, hb', hval2, hr'⟩ := epad_val_run (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z y true C d
        Sum.inl (.inr .q1T) (.inr .no) (fun _ => rfl)
        (fun j hj => by
          rw [show epadS true * j = 2 * j from rfl, (epadIn_answer z _).1, hz, pairEncode_getD,
            if_pos (by omega), show 2 * j / 2 = j by omega])
        ((C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1)) (by omega) v hv h0 h1 hzr
      by_cases hvy : epadValid C d y
      · rw [if_pos hvy] at hr'
        obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hvy
        have hfst : pairFstD y = a := by rw [ha, pairFstD_pairEncode]
        have hya : y.length = 2 * a.length + 2 + C * (a.length + 1) ^ d := by
          rw [ha, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
        have hpost := epad_bank_post C d mode z ((C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1))
          a.length (LogProg.bitsVal w) v' hb' (by rw [hval2 ⟨a, ha⟩, hfst])
          (by rw [hfr 13 (by decide), h13]) (by rw [hfr 15 (by decide), h15])
          (by rw [hfr 16 (by decide), h16]) (by rw [hfr 17 (by decide), h17]) (by omega)
        have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z =
            (if LogProg.bitsVal w < a.length then
              (if mode then z.getD (4 * LogProg.bitsVal w) false else true) else false) := by
          rw [indicator_eq_decide]
          have hm := epad_mem_Q_iff (C := C) (d := d) (mode := mode) hd
          rw [hfst] at hm
          by_cases hi : LogProg.bitsVal w < a.length
          · rw [if_pos hi]
            cases mode with
            | false =>
              exact decide_eq_true (hm.mpr ⟨hw.1, hw.2, ⟨a, ha⟩, by simpa using hi⟩)
            | true =>
              have h4 : z.getD (4 * LogProg.bitsVal w) false = a.getD (LogProg.bitsVal w) false :=
                by rw [hz, ha, epad_getD_four a _ w _ hi]
              rw [if_pos rfl, h4]
              cases hb : a.getD (LogProg.bitsVal w) false
              · refine decide_eq_false (fun h => ?_)
                have h5 := (hm.mp h).2.2.2
                rw [if_pos rfl, hb] at h5
                exact Bool.false_ne_true h5
              · exact decide_eq_true (hm.mpr ⟨hw.1, hw.2, ⟨a, ha⟩, by rw [if_pos rfl]; exact hb⟩)
          · rw [if_neg hi]
            refine decide_eq_false (fun h => ?_)
            have h4 := (hm.mp h).2.2.2
            cases mode with
            | false => exact hi (by simpa using h4)
            | true =>
              simp only [if_true] at h4
              rw [List.getD_eq_default _ _ (by omega)] at h4
              exact Bool.false_ne_true h4
        rw [hans]
        exact hr.halt (hr'.halt hpost)
      · rw [if_neg hvy] at hr'
        have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z = false := by
          rw [indicator_eq_decide]
          exact decide_eq_false (fun h => hvy ((epad_mem_Q_iff hd).mp h).2.2.1)
        rw [hans]
        exact hr.halt (hr'.halt (hno v' hb'))
    · obtain ⟨v, hv, hr⟩ := hbad hw
      have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z = false := by
        rw [indicator_eq_decide]
        exact decide_eq_false (fun h => hw ⟨((epad_mem_Q_iff hd).mp h).1,
          ((epad_mem_Q_iff hd).mp h).2.1⟩)
      rw [hans]
      exact hr.halt (hno v hv)

/-! ### The run phase (E-PAD checkpoint 3) -/

/-- **The run phase** (checkpoint 3): the oracle-input simulator runs `L`'s decider on the
virtual input `epadVirt y`, answered by the bank, within `K · T |y|` work cells, on every input.

**Proof sketch.** `LogProg.OIS.compile_decides` with `L`'s decider `M` (space `c · S`) and the
bank `![M₀, M₁]` of `epadQ`'s deciders (space `c_j · logSpace`), whose laws on genuine queries
are `epad_query_mem_iff`. With `m = |y|` and `v = epadVirt y`: on a padded `y = ⟨a, 1^{…}⟩`,
`m = 2|a| + 2 + C (|a| + 1)^d`, so `S |v| ≤ T m` by `hST`; otherwise `v = []` and
`S 0 ≤ S 0 · T m`. The index register costs `|bits (|v| + 1)| + 2 ≤ 4 T m` and the bank
`k_D (2B + 1)` with `B = (c₀ + c₁)(3m + 4) + 1`, so `2B + 1 ≤ (8 (c₀ + c₁) + 3) T m`. -/
private theorem epad_run {L : Language Bool} {S T : ℕ → ℕ} (C d : ℕ) (hL : L ∈ SPACE S)
    (hST : ∀ n, S n ≤ T (2 * n + 2 + C * (n + 1) ^ d)) (hT : ∀ m, m + 1 ≤ T m) :
    ∃ (K : ℕ) (O : FinTM Bool), O.ComputesInSpace
      (fun y => [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) (epadVirt C d y)])
      (fun n => K * T n) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨c, M, hM⟩ := mem_SPACE_iff.mp hL
  have hQ0 := epad_Q_mem C d false
  have hQ1 := epad_Q_mem C d true
  rw [LOGSPACE_eq, mem_SPACE_iff] at hQ0 hQ1
  obtain ⟨c0, M0, h0⟩ := hQ0
  obtain ⟨c1, M1, h1⟩ := hQ1
  let Ms : Fin 2 → FinTM Bool := ![M0, M1]
  let As : Fin 2 → Language Bool := ![epadQ C d false, epadQ C d true]
  let sb : Fin 2 → ℕ → ℕ := ![fun n => c0 * logSpace n, fun n => c1 * logSpace n]
  have hMs : ∀ j, (Ms j).DecidesInSpace (As j) (sb j) := by
    intro j
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => Fin.elim0 i)) j
    · show M0.DecidesInSpace (epadQ C d false) (fun n => c0 * logSpace n)
      exact h0
    · show M1.DecidesInSpace (epadQ C d true) (fun n => c1 * logSpace n)
      exact h1
  have hsb : ∀ j q, sb j q ≤ (c0 + c1) * (q + 1) := by
    intro j q
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => Fin.elim0 i)) j
    · show c0 * logSpace q ≤ (c0 + c1) * (q + 1)
      exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_add_right _ _) (logSpace_le_succ q)
    · show c1 * logSpace q ≤ (c0 + c1) * (q + 1)
      exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_add_left _ _) (logSpace_le_succ q)
  refine ⟨M.k * (2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) + 4 +
      (LogProg.bankK Ms + LogProg.bankK Ms) * (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3),
    LogProg.compileFinTM (LogProg.OIS.prog M) (LogProg.OIS.start M) (LogProg.bankTM Ms)
      (LogProg.bankStart Ms), ?_⟩
  rw [FinTM.computesInSpace_iff]
  intro y
  set v := epadVirt C d y with hv
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hs⟩ :=
    (FinTM.computesInSpace_iff _ _ _).mp ((FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff _ _ _).mp hM) v
  have hvm : v.length ≤ y.length := epadVirt_length_le C d y
  set B := (c0 + c1) * (3 * y.length + 4) + 1 with hB
  have hbits : ∀ i ≤ v.length, (Nat.bits i).length ≤ y.length + 1 := by
    intro i hi
    have h1 := LogProg.length_bits_le_log i
    have h2 := Nat.log_le_self 2 i
    omega
  have hBnd : ∀ j, ∀ i ≤ v.length,
      max (sb j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits i)).length) 1 ≤ B := by
    intro j i hi
    have hq := hsb j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits i)).length
    rw [length_pairEncode] at hq ⊢
    have hb := hbits i hi
    have hmono : (c0 + c1) * (2 * y.length + 2 + (Nat.bits i).length + 1) ≤
        (c0 + c1) * (3 * y.length + 4) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
    refine max_le ?_ (by omega)
    omega
  have hA0 : ∀ i ≤ v.length,
      pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ As 0 ↔ i < v.length := by
    intro i hi
    show pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ epadQ C d false ↔ i < v.length
    rw [epad_query_mem_iff C d false y i (hi.trans hvm)]
    simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_valid hval]
      exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hval, h⟩⟩
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_not_valid hval]
      exact ⟨fun h => absurd h.1 hval, fun h => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)⟩
  have hA1 : ∀ i < v.length,
      pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ As 1 ↔ v.getD i false = true := by
    intro i hi
    show pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ epadQ C d true ↔ v.getD i false = true
    rw [epad_query_mem_iff C d true y i (hi.le.trans hvm)]
    simp only [if_true]
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_valid hval]
      exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hval, h⟩⟩
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_not_valid hval] at hi
      exact absurd hi (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  obtain ⟨T', hT', hSp⟩ := LogProg.OIS.compile_decides M Ms As sb hMs y v
    [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) v] hA0 hA1 t ht B hBnd
  refine ⟨T', hT', hSp.trans ?_⟩
  -- the space ledger
  have hTm := hT y.length
  have hS : S v.length ≤ (S 0 + 1) * T y.length := by
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hval
      have hva : v.length = a.length := by
        rw [hv, epadVirt_of_valid ⟨a, ha⟩, ha, pairFstD_pairEncode]
      have hma : y.length = 2 * a.length + 2 + C * (a.length + 1) ^ d := by
        rw [ha, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
      rw [hva]
      have h1 := hST a.length
      rw [← hma] at h1
      calc S a.length ≤ T y.length := h1
        _ ≤ (S 0 + 1) * T y.length := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ (Nat.succ_pos _)
    · have hv0 : v.length = 0 := by rw [hv, epadVirt_of_not_valid hval]; rfl
      rw [hv0]
      calc S 0 ≤ S 0 * T y.length := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
        _ ≤ (S 0 + 1) * T y.length := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ _)
  have hsp : M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg v) t ≤ c * ((S 0 + 1) * T y.length) :=
    hs.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left c hS)
  have hW : (Nat.bits (v.length + 1)).length + 2 ≤ 4 * T y.length := by
    have h1 := LogProg.length_bits_le_log (v.length + 1)
    have h2 := Nat.log_le_self 2 (v.length + 1)
    omega
  have h2B : 2 * B + 1 ≤ (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length := by
    have h1 : (c0 + c1) * (3 * y.length + 4) ≤ (c0 + c1) * (4 * T y.length) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
    have e : (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length =
        2 * ((c0 + c1) * (4 * T y.length)) + 3 * T y.length := by ring
    rw [e, hB]
    omega
  have hk1 : M.k * (2 * M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg v) t + 1) ≤
      M.k * ((2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) * T y.length) := by
    apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
    have e : (2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) * T y.length =
        2 * (c * ((S 0 + 1) * T y.length)) + T y.length := by ring
    rw [e]
    omega
  set kD := LogProg.bankK Ms + LogProg.bankK Ms with hkD
  have hk2 : kD * (2 * B + 1) ≤ kD * ((8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length) :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ h2B
  have e : (M.k * (2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) + 4 + kD * (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3)) * T y.length =
      M.k * ((2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) * T y.length) + 4 * T y.length +
        kD * ((8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length) := by ring
  rw [e]
  omega

/-- **Padding transfers space bounds down** ([AB09, Exercise 3.2], the padding argument in space
form): if `L ∈ SPACE S`, then the language of `L`'s members padded by `C · (|x| + 1)^d` ones lies
in `SPACE T` for every `T` with `m + 1 ≤ T m` (room to validate the padding and to copy the first
component) and `S n ≤ T (2n + 2 + C (n + 1)^d)` (room for `L`'s decider, at the padded length
`|pairEncode x 1^{C (|x|+1)^d}| = 2|x| + 2 + C (|x| + 1)^d`).

**Proof sketch.** Let `M` decide `L` within `c · S` cells. On input `y`, first check that `y` is a
pair `pairEncode x w` whose second component `w` consists of exactly `C (|x| + 1)^d` ones;
reject otherwise. That needs `O(log |y|) ⊆ O(|y| + 1)` cells, on malformed inputs too, and never
writes the pad. Then run `M` on `x`, read in place as a virtual input, and answer as `M` does,
within `c · S |x|` cells for `M` plus `O(|y| + 1)` for the simulation. For a validated `y`,
`|y| = 2|x| + 2 + C (|x| + 1)^d`, so `S |x| ≤ T |y|`, and both phases fit in `O(T |y|)`.

**Implementation.** Three machines and the catalog's conditional
(`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond_spaceUsed`): the validator decides the padded words in
logarithmic space (`epad_V_mem`, an abstract register machine through
`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_poly`); on a padded word the run phase (`epad_run`) runs `M`
through the oracle-input simulator `Complexity.LogProg.OIS.compile_decides` on the virtual
input `epadVirt y` (the first component of a padded word, `[]` otherwise), whose length and bit
queries a bank of two logspace deciders answers (`epad_Q_mem`); otherwise the constant `[false]`
machine answers. The run phase's space is
`M.k (2 c S |v| + 1) + |bits (|v| + 1)| + 2 + k_D (2B + 1)` with `B = O(|y| + 1)`;
`S |v| ≤ (S 0 + 1) T |y|` both on padded words (by `hST`) and off them (`v = []`), and
`|y| + 1 ≤ T |y|` absorbs the rest. -/
theorem mem_SPACE_padLang {L : Language Bool} {S T : ℕ → ℕ} (C d : ℕ) (hL : L ∈ SPACE S)
    (hST : ∀ n, S n ≤ T (2 * n + 2 + C * (n + 1) ^ d)) (hT : ∀ m, m + 1 ≤ T m) :
    padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) ∈ SPACE T := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨K, O, hO⟩ := epad_run C d hL hST hT
  have hV := epad_V_mem C d
  rw [LOGSPACE_eq, mem_SPACE_iff] at hV
  obtain ⟨cV, D, hD⟩ := hV
  rw [FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff] at hD
  obtain ⟨hDt, hDs⟩ := hD.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le
  obtain ⟨hOt, hOs⟩ := hO.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le
  obtain ⟨Mf, cf, hMf, hMfs⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_const_spaceUsed [false]
  obtain ⟨Mc, cc, hMc, hMcs⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond_spaceUsed
    (p := fun y => MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) y)
    (fun n => cV * logSpace n) (fun n => K * T n) (fun _ => cf) hDt hOt hMf hDs hOs hMfs
  rw [mem_SPACE_iff]
  refine ⟨cV + K + cf + cc, Mc, ?_⟩
  rw [FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff, FinTM.computesInSpace_iff]
  intro y
  have hout : (if MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) y = true then
      [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) (epadVirt C d y)] else [false]) =
      [MultiTapeTM.indicator (padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) : Set (List Bool)) y] := by
    rw [LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, LogProg.indicator_eq_decide]
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · have hmem : y ∈ (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) := epad_mem_V.mpr hval
      rw [epadVirt_of_valid hval]
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hval
      have hpad : y ∈ (padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) : Set (List Bool)) ↔
          pairFstD y ∈ (L : Set (List Bool)) := by
        rw [ha, pairFstD_pairEncode]
        constructor
        · intro h
          obtain ⟨x, hx, hxe⟩ := mem_padLang_iff.mp h
          have := congrArg pairFstD hxe
          rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode] at this
          rw [this]; exact hx
        · intro h
          exact mem_padLang_iff.mpr ⟨a, h, rfl⟩
      simp only [hmem, decide_true, if_true, List.cons.injEq, and_true]
      exact decide_eq_decide.mpr hpad.symm
    · have hmem : y ∉ (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) := fun h => hval (epad_mem_V.mp h)
      have hpad : y ∉ (padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) : Set (List Bool)) := by
        intro h
        obtain ⟨x, -, hxe⟩ := mem_padLang_iff.mp h
        exact hval ⟨x, hxe⟩
      simp only [hmem, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, hpad]
  have hc := (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp hMc y
  rw [hout] at hc
  refine ⟨_, hc, (hMcs y _).trans ?_⟩
  have hTy := hT y.length
  have h1 : cV * logSpace y.length ≤ cV * T y.length :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ ((logSpace_le_succ _).trans hTy)
  have h2 : max (K * T y.length) cf ≤ K * T y.length + cf * T y.length :=
    max_le (Nat.le_add_right _ _) (le_add_left (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)))
  have h3 : cc ≤ cc * T y.length := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  have e : (cV + K + cf + cc) * T y.length =
      cV * T y.length + K * T y.length + cf * T y.length + cc * T y.length := by ring
  rw [e]
  omega

end Complexity

## ===== campaign/fills/epad/reviews/epad-fill/internal-review.md =====

# Internal incoming-delivery review: E-PAD

I read **all 1,762 lines** of the delivered `src/TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean`, plus the brief, the report's substantive claims, the supplied axiom-walk source/output, both final control sources, the seal list/exemptions, and the four patch headers. Delivered source SHA-256: `7590aaa2b1a5eb5d40dfe5b653cddb47fa8cf7b5ea85e03b8f923ade1eae2467`. Line references below are to that unchanged delivered source, not the maintainer's landing edits.

This is a static internal review. I ran the campaign's comment-aware declaration comparison and its trusted policy linter on an isolated copy, and inspected repository/Mathlib source. **I did not run Lean/Lake, execute delivered tools, run copy-text screens, edit delivery/repository source, commit, or push.** The agent's compilation/seal/screen statements remain attributed delivery claims until the maintainer replays them.

## Confirmed repairs

| Item | Delivered location | Finding and mechanical resolution |
|---|---|---|
| R1, semantic reuse | `Padding.lean:1205–1213`, used once at `1389` | `epad_two_pow_bits` states exactly `2 ^ |bits n| ≤ 2*n+1`, already public as `Randomized.PolyAmp.two_pow_bits_le`; its positive branch also re-derives the reachable `LogProg.two_pow_bits_le`. The REPORT's "no published counterpart" claim is false. Delete the private helper and prove the actual decoder cap in `hval` directly: split on `y.length = 0`; handle zero by `Nat.zero_bits`, and use `LogProg.two_pow_bits_le y.length` for the positive branch, followed by the existing cap arithmetic. This avoids both a new import and a dependency on unmerged #222. |
| R2, inline semantic reuse | `1590–1594` and `1651–1654` | `hbits` and `hW` derive bit-length upper bounds through `length_bits_le_log` plus `Nat.log_le_self`. The already reachable stronger `Turing.length_bits_le_self` supplies each binary-length step directly. Keep the surrounding hypotheses/omega arithmetic and cite that lemma. These are BL-1 (iii)'s kind. |
| R3, pending-PR compatibility | code `1386`; explanatory citation `1225` | The explicit name `Codec.bitsVal_lt_two_pow` disappears in #222. Its canonical, statement-identical original `LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow` already exists at the current campaign and the fill base. Re-point the one code use and the corresponding source docstring; no import or statement change is needed. Preserve the delivered REPORT verbatim and explain the landing change separately. |
| R4, compiler-constant accounting | REPORT §4/§8 versus `evidence/logs/axioms-final.log:6–8` | The report says the module's non-private constants are exactly the base's three. Its own unfiltered module walk lists six: the three public declarations plus `Complexity.mem_SPACE_padLang._proof_1_1`, `._proof_1_2`, `._proof_1_3`. These are compiler proof auxiliaries, not new public declarations. Report them separately under root `workflow.md` §4; this is an accounting correction, not an API violation. |
| R5, new proof sketches | declaration starts `194`, `303`, `381`, `631` | The policy linter finds four new long private proofs without `**Proof sketch.**`: `epad_ones_loop`, `epad_mul_loop`, `epad_pow_loop`, `epad_val_run`. Add sketches beside them. The size finding is informational under the campaign's no-size-driver rule. |
| R6, source prose | `65`, `147–148`, `953`, `991`, `1441`, `1539–1541`; old module text `34–42` | New section/docstring text carries campaign/checkpoint provenance. Remove those labels from Lean prose. The frozen module's old "Statement; its proof is a fill" and copying description are stale after the virtual-input proof; update them in the maintainer landing while preserving the delivered source/report as evidence. |

The reuse repairs above fit the standing mechanical re-pointing rule: they need no public API, theorem statement, rename, import, or new debt acknowledgment.

## Freeze, ownership and architecture

- The trusted `declfreeze.py` comparison against the current campaign reports **3 → 3 public declarations, 0 → 50 private**, zero public additions/removals, zero statement changes, and only the authorized body change of `Complexity.mem_SPACE_padLang`. All new source declarations use the allowed prefixes. The local tactic macro is section-scoped.
- All four delivered patch headers touch only `TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean`. This is a source-header check; the maintainer should still verify the bundle/patch correspondence before applying it.
- Added imports are `Logspace/PreimageHost`, `Build/Catalog`, `ClassNP/PolyTimePairing`, and `Codec/Word`. A source import-graph walk found 88 nodes including Padding, no cycle and no path to Hierarchy.
- The architecture consumes the published `OIS.compile_decides` host and catalog conditional/constant rows. The validator and bank are concrete deciders assembled from published ARM loops. The generic multiplication/powering helpers compute arithmetic leaf values; the ones scan is a leaf word check. **I found no confirmed new private host requiring a design ruling.**
- I inspected `Codec.scan_loop` (`Codec/Engine.lean:97`): it requires two oracle reads and two lockstep pointer advances per iteration and returns a finite-state fold. It is not a direct instantiation for the delivered one-read/one-counter-increment early-failure ones scan. The available `ARMLoops` rows provide move/copy/fixed-shift/subtract/halve, not the delivered register-factor/power contract. Replacing the whole validator route to use a different scanner would be a design change, not a missing mechanical citation found here.

## Seal assessment and unresolved execution

The final delivered list seals 36 foreign definitions, including `astep`, `AReach`, `AHalt`, `PreS`, space predicates, the oracle-input compiler/bank definitions, pairing, and `bitsVal`. The unsealed and sealed control sources differ by the seal block; their shared meta command elaborates the same first defining equation with `intros; rfl` under `Term.withoutErrToSorry`. The supplied combined log contains **36 `rfl closes` and 36 `rfl FAILS`** messages. This is a credible static control design, not a maintainer execution result.

`ARM`, `AConf` and `BankS` are source-verified `abbrev`s, and the FinTM exclusions are structure projections. The generated `Ins` eliminator and `alignedPair_loop.match_1` exemptions are explicitly disclosed; the latter reduces the match appearing in a published theorem's statement. I found no source argument explicitly unfolding another-file TCSlib or Core/Mathlib definition in the new proof. Own-file definitions are read directly, as allowed.

**Unresolved:** the maintainer must execute the final merged-tree module, facade, fresh axiom/public-constant walk, sealed source and positive/negative controls after the landing repairs. I have not independently reproduced those outcomes. The matcher exemption and the general exclusion list should be visible in the gate; I found no additional confirmed seal hole from this source review.

The mathematical assembly handles malformed inputs by making their virtual input empty and charges `S 0` as a constant. It uses neither monotonicity nor computability of `S`/`T`; initialization and all bank tapes appear in the space ledger. I found no statement-level obstruction or missing-boundary-case issue on this static reading.

# E-PAD incoming-delivery review and landing repairs

Delivery commit: `7d16731e963f60a4ba97e79ec7dba41c86dca1bb`. Landing repair commits: `3a0cb27fe50868317ced9710769add53036f52e8` and `b6c2f5e4b8ce3bc18c385a09a3bf5dc26b75c205`.
PR: [#228](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/pull/228), based on `complexity/arora-barak-ch3-4`.
Gate 115 is reserved; it has not been dispatched. **Not yet clear to merge.**

## Evidence handling

The pinned exchange archive passed all 118 payload checksums, path/size/symlink checks, and the outer REPORT comparison (`receipt.json`). The Git bundle verifies and matches the delivered source. Four patches were applied with `git am -3` on the current campaign, preserving the original authors and using Codex as committer. Only `SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean` changes. The original delivered source is retained as `delivery/Padding.lean.txt`.

The maintainer read all 1,762 delivered library-source lines before elaboration. A separate internal review also read the complete source; it ran no Lean or delivered tooling. Its findings are retained verbatim in `internal-review.md` (SHA-256 `f5c9db8a84ee464b348f48909ad1640f67daaf86b4110dc81935efefb8d9cc26`). The delivered REPORT is retained verbatim (SHA-256 `238582d877084f606af224e7d5768a2046d8f5877d7ae6ac4895fc9f284a9767`); its claims are attributed to the delivering agent, not converted into maintainer attestations. No delivered shell or Python tool was executed.

## Dispositions of the internal findings

| Item | Disposition in the landing repair |
|---|---|
| R1, duplicate `2^|bits n|` bound | Deleted `epad_two_pow_bits`. The decoder cap now splits at zero and cites the already reachable `LogProg.two_pow_bits_le` for the positive case. It uses no unmerged NatBits declaration. |
| R2, two inline binary-length bounds | Both now cite `Turing.length_bits_le_self`, with the existing surrounding inequalities. |
| R3, name removed by NatBits | Code and explanatory prose cite the canonical `LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow`. Removed the now-unneeded `Codec.Word` import. This makes either PR's merge order possible without that deleted explicit name. |
| R4, non-private-constant count | The REPORT's three source declarations are correct, but its claim of only three non-private constants is contradicted by its own axiom log: `mem_SPACE_padLang._proof_1_1`, `._proof_1_2`, `._proof_1_3` are also present. They are compiler-generated proof auxiliaries. The original report is unchanged; the fresh landing census confirms six non-private constants (three source declarations and three internal proof auxiliaries); all 506 compiled constants use only the standard three axioms. |
| R5, proof sketches | Added substantive English sketches to `epad_ones_loop`, `epad_mul_loop`, `epad_pow_loop` and `epad_val_run`. |
| R6, source prose | Removed new checkpoint/campaign provenance and corrected the old statement-only/copying description to describe the completed virtual-input proof. Mathematical statements remain frozen. |

The maintainer also replaced two zero-case update-extensionality blocks in `epad_mul_loop` and `epad_pow_loop` with `Function.update_eq_self` and arithmetic equations. These are the existing identity-update facts, used directly through the published Mathlib API.

The current source census is **3 → 3 public source declarations, 0 → 49 private**; no public additions/removals, no statement changes, no surviving public/private order changes, and only the authorized public proof body changes. The delivered source had 50 privates before R1's deletion. Current size: **1,769 lines**. The policy linter reports only size; size is not a split or delay driver under WORKFLOW §2.

## Architecture and remaining execution

The virtual input is empty on malformed words. The validator and the two bank languages use concrete register machines; the run phase uses the published `OIS.compile_decides` host; the final conditional rejects invalid padding. The constant `S 0` is absorbed by the linear lower bound on `T`, without monotonicity or computability assumptions on the bound functions. The internal source review found no new private host needing a design ruling.

The review's supplied seal inventory has 36 definitions and explicitly excludes abbreviations, projections, one generated eliminator and a matcher in a published statement. Maintainer probes are prepared, including a first-equation and parameter-abstracted-equation control for each definition. The module plus three boundary probes pass; the independent replay passes two modules with zero failures/static mismatches; all 506 constants use only the standard axioms; all 72 controls close unsealed and fail sealed. The fresh walk partitions 46 foreign definitions into the 36 effective seals and ten explicit exclusions, and all 122 citations from 20 modules are covered by the 23-file screen population. The matcher limitation and four reducibility rejections were reproduced. Gate 115 contains the exact inputs, outputs and cross-checks.

The follow-up Core list-equation repair preserves the reduced import set after removing Codec.Word. Its initial failed preflight is retained separately. The final gate evidence, not the original delivery report, is the authority for the landing execution results.

## ===== campaign/gates/110-epad-statements/pack.md =====

# External audit pack: the E-PAD statements, `Complexity.mem_SPACE_padLang` (PR #219, a statement gate)

## Why this PR

B6's H fill (#218, gate 109) proved `space_hierarchy` and ended `SPACE_linear_ne_NP`
([AB09, Exercise 3.2]) in the named escalation **E-PAD**. The library has no host for the
padded-language space decider. The user ruled on 2026-11-06:
- E-PAD's API publishes a **general** lemma (any space bound, a polynomial unary pad);
- it goes in a **new `SpaceComplexity/Padding`** module, for later reuse by Ladner's padding;
- `Hierarchy` may import it, and the maintainer then closes `SPACE_linear_ne_NP` in a small PR.

This PR lands the **statements only**. The proof of `mem_SPACE_padLang` is a fill, briefed after
this gate closes.

**The PR:** #219 on `lean/epad-statements`, head `7cd74fff` (full hash in the bundle header). It
consists of the change `b635f73b` and merges of the campaign. It adds
`TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean` (77 lines) and its line in the
`SpaceComplexity` facade.

## The statements (verify)

```lean
def padLang (L : Language Bool) (pad : ℕ → ℕ) : Language Bool :=
  {y | ∃ x ∈ L, y = pairEncode x (List.replicate (pad x.length) true)}

theorem mem_padLang_iff {L : Language Bool} {pad : ℕ → ℕ} {y : List Bool} :
    y ∈ padLang L pad ↔ ∃ x ∈ L, y = pairEncode x (List.replicate (pad x.length) true) :=
  Iff.rfl

theorem mem_SPACE_padLang {L : Language Bool} {S T : ℕ → ℕ} (C d : ℕ) (hL : L ∈ SPACE S)
    (hST : ∀ n, S n ≤ T (2 * n + 2 + C * (n + 1) ^ d)) (hT : ∀ m, m + 1 ≤ T m) :
    padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) ∈ SPACE T := by
  sorry
```

All three are in namespace `Complexity`. The module imports `SpaceComplexity/Basic` only, which
brings in `SPACE` and, through `Encoding`, `pairEncode`. `|pairEncode x w| = 2|x| + 2 + |w|`
(`Turing.length_pairEncode`), so the padded length is `2n + 2 + C (n + 1)^d`.

**Why it should be true (the fill's route, in the docstring's sketch).** Let `M` decide `L` in
`c · S` cells. On input `y`:
1. Check that `y` is `pairEncode x w` with `w = 1^{C (|x|+1)^d}`, and reject otherwise. This
   needs `O(|y|)` cells, which `hT` pays for at every length, valid or not.
2. Run `M` on `x`, copied or read through a bounded input device, within `c · S |x|` cells,
   which `hST` pays for at the padded length.

`DecidesInSpace` asks for `O(T |y|)` on every input. Invalid inputs cost only the check.

## Brief for the auditor

1. **Truth and form:** is `mem_SPACE_padLang` true as stated, for every `S`, `T`, `C` and `d`?
   Check in particular:
   - `C = 0` and `d = 0`;
   - a non-monotone `T`;
   - invalid inputs;
   - the empty `x`;
   - that `DecidesInSpace` needs the bound at every input length.

   Are the hypotheses the natural ones? Is anything stronger than needed in a way that would
   block the reuse the ruling intends (Ladner's padding, which is time-based and would need its
   own statement)?
2. **The consumer:** does the statement give exactly the hypothesis that `Hierarchy`'s private
   `sph_linear_ne_NP_of_padding` consumes at `S n = n² + 1`, `T n = n + 1`, `C = 1` and `d = 2`?
   Answer through `mem_padLang_iff` only, with no unfolding of `padLang` (rule 10);
   `evidence/probe/`.
3. **Public text:** are the docstrings accurate and attributed, and is the module docstring
   complete?

## Repository-side attestations (verify or challenge)

- **Consumer probe** (`evidence/probe/EPadProbe.lean.txt`, `.out`). The probe:
  - copies the module's text inline;
  - derives `sph_linear_ne_NP_of_padding`'s `hpad` hypothesis from `mem_SPACE_padLang`
    through `mem_padLang_iff` and `Set.ext`, with `n² + 1 ≤ 2n + 2 + (n + 1)² + 1` from
    `Nat.pow_le_pow_left` and `omega`;
  - instantiates the edge case `C = 0`, `d = 0`;
  - prints `mem_padLang_iff`'s axioms.

  It elaborates with **exit 0**. The only `sorry` warning is the statement's own, and
  `mem_padLang_iff` depends on no axioms.
- **Replay** (`evidence/merged-tree/`): `replay-lep2` at `7cd74fff` (the new module and the
  facade), chained from the campaign snapshot after #216: **2 modules, 0 failed**. The one
  `sorry` warning is `mem_SPACE_padLang`'s. The static check finds 0 mismatches. #217 and #211
  merged afterwards. Neither touches `Padding`'s import closure (`SpaceComplexity/Basic` and
  upstream).
- **Lint** (`evidence/lint/`):
  - The policy linter on `Padding` gives 0 findings.
  - The campaign lint on `SpaceComplexity` gives 0 FAIL, 82 WARN over 113 files. The one new
    WARN is check 8 ("public def without a lemma beside it: `padLang`"). That check recognizes
    only `padLang_…` names. The definition's published characterization is
    `mem_padLang_iff`, in the `mem_SPACE_iff` pattern of `SpaceComplexity/Basic`. This is
    disclosed.

## Findings format

| # | Severity | File · declaration | Claim | Evidence / counterexample | Proposed fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The severity guide is in `campaign/standards/TEMPLATE.md`. Findings are copied verbatim into
`campaign/gates/110-epad-statements/findings.md`. The gate closes when it has zero blockers and
zero majors.

**Deliver your findings as a downloadable Markdown file named `epad-statements-findings.md`** (the
findings table and the verdict line, no other wrapping), and also paste its content in your reply.

| 3 | note | `SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean:12–59` · public text, `padLang`, `mem_padLang_iff` | The definition and its reading lemma have the intended meaning. | In mathematical English, the language contains exactly the encodings obtained by taking a member of `L`, doubling each of its bits, appending the separator `[false, true]`, then appending the prescribed number of `true` bits. It excludes every other word. `pairDecode_pairEncode` and `pairEncode_injective` establish unique recovery; `length_pairEncode` gives the stated length. `mem_padLang_iff` expresses precisely this membership condition, and its `Iff.rfl` proof needs no axioms. The module has all required headings, attribution, and an explicit pending-proof notice. [Arora's reproduction of Exercise 3.2](https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall10/cos487/hw5.pdf), Problem 2, confirms the separation being supported; the pairing is the library's encoding convention. | Optional sanity lemma: `pairEncode x (List.replicate (pad x.length) true) ∈ padLang L pad ↔ x ∈ L`, using `mem_padLang_iff` and pairing injectivity. For precise documentation, cite `pairDecode_pairEncode` for recovery in lines 35–36, alongside the length theorem. |
| 4 | note | `SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean:72` · `mem_SPACE_padLang` | The sorried statement is mathematically true as stated. | Obtain a fixed finite decider from `hL`, using at most `c · S n` work cells. On an input of length `m`, parse the pair and validate its all-`true` suffix using binary counters and polynomial arithmetic capped at `m + 1`; this takes `O(m + 1)` space, including malformed inputs, without constructing the proposed pad. For a valid word, retain its first component of length `n` and simulate the fixed decider with total space `O(m + 1 + c · S n)`, halting because that decider is total. The exact identity `m = 2n + 2 + C(n + 1)^d`, followed by `hST` and `hT`, bounds this by one constant times `T m`; invalid words are rejected within the same bound. This is a semantic correctness argument: the finite-machine construction and its Lean proof remain the advertised fill. | No statement change. In the fill, account explicitly for initialization and the simulated input; `O(m + 1)` states the validation bound uniformly at length zero. |
| 5 | note | `SpaceComplexity/Padding.lean` · adversarial instances | The boundary cases do not require extra hypotheses. | **Zero padding:** `C = 0`, for every `d`, gives an empty suffix and length `2n + 2`. **Constant padding:** `d = 0` gives exactly `C` ones and length `2n + 2 + C`. **Empty first component:** its pad has length `C`, since `(0 + 1)^d = 1`, so its encoding has length `C + 2` and belongs exactly when `[] ∈ L`. **Invalid inputs:** `[]` and `[true, false]` cannot be pairs; with `C = 1, d = 2`, `pairEncode [] [false]` has the correct length but must still be rejected. **Non-monotone target:** take `S n = n + 1`, `C = d = 0`, and `T m = m + 1 + (if Even m then 100 else 0)`; both hypotheses hold although `T 0 = 101 > 2 = T 1`. No monotonicity is used. Zeros in `S` restrict the source class under `Basic.lean`'s convention but do not invalidate the implication; `hT` guarantees positive target space at every length. | None. |
| 6 | note | `Hierarchy.lean:2325` · `sph_linear_ne_NP_of_padding`; `evidence/probe/` | The API supplies exactly the consumer's `hpad`, without unfolding `padLang`. | Instantiate `S n = n² + 1`, `T m = m + 1`, `C = 1`, `d = 2`. The required inequality is `n² + 1 ≤ 2n + 2 + (n + 1)² + 1 = n² + 4n + 4`; `hT` is reflexivity. `Set.ext` with `mem_padLang_iff` identifies the resulting language with the consumer's literal set, including its `1 *` factor. The probe's inline module text matches the source, and its consumer proof uses this characterization only. Its second example instantiates `C = d = 0`; `EPadProbe.out` records exit 0, one warning for `mem_SPACE_padLang`, and no axioms for `mem_padLang_iff`. Lean elaboration was not independently rerun here. | None for the statement gate. Apply the API in the planned consumer follow-up after the fill. |
| 7 | note | `mem_SPACE_padLang` · hypotheses and future reuse | The hypotheses are sufficient and suitably general for this consumer, with a deliberate restriction to at-least-linear target space and fixed polynomial padding. | Neither `S` nor `T` must be computable, constructible, or monotone: the decider never evaluates them. The everywhere-linear `hT` is stronger than necessary for some languages, but pays for validation and copying on all inputs and admits the intended linear target. `padLang` itself accepts any padding function. Ladner's variable-exponent, time-based padding still needs its own complexity statement; the roadmap's literal `ψ ++ false :: true^(...)` also needs an encoding translation if this paired-language definition is reused. These are future interface obligations, not defects in the present implication. | Preserve the present statement. Make the time bound and encoding choice explicit in Ladner's own statement gate. |
| 8 | note | `evidence/merged-tree/` · replay attestation | The supplied replay evidence is consistent with the pinned source and import graph. | The script's blob pins match `Padding.lean` (`39a59037fb3b7582ef154cd8819640ac05c1b6ea`) and the facade (`2c7a771f631cd96ffdb58fc6db20db75d54a0ed4`). This attestation establishes statement elaboration, not a proof of the admitted theorem. |
